title: Director, Market Operations
description:
Director, Market Operations

ArchWell Health is a new, innovative healthcare provider devoted to improving the lives of our senior members. We deliver best-in-class care at comfortable, accessible neighborhood clinics where seniors can feel at home and become part of a vibrant, wellness-focused community. Our members experience greater continuity of care, as well as the comfort of knowing they will be treated with respect by people who genuinely care about them, their families, and their communities.

Job Summary:

The Director, Market Operations is the primary business leader responsible for all ArchWell Health centers in a metropolitan area. They are responsible for achieving the market’s financial objectives while achieving superior employee and patient satisfaction. This role reports to the National Vice President of Operations and works hand-in-hand with a clinical peer, the Market Medical Director. In addition to hiring & managing a team of adept Center Managers who ensure excellence in center operations and membership experience, the Operations Director has market oversight for other non-clinical functions like Growth and Network, which report into the Market Growth Manager and Market Network Manager, respectively. The Director, Market Operations is a critical, multi-disciplinary leader at the heart of any market’s success.

This leader should be a strong communicator who builds relationships quickly and is passionate about working in a fast-paced, results-driven organization. A track record of building strong cohesive teams with a member-first and operational sustainability mentality is a must-have.

Duties/Responsibilities:

Implement market launch plan in partnership with ArchWell Health’s corporate Growth team; this includes hiring and training Center Managers, setting up core management processes, and building a culture of operational excellence and teamwork
Provide leadership and P&L management over the market, responsible for all center operations across the market and achieving financial, growth, and operational KPIs; there is a significant focus on growth and member satisfaction

Organize the market leadership team around shared objectives regularly; manage weekly market leadership team meetings and ensures leadership is focused on the right issues; sets appropriate financial/operational/quality performance goals
Provide local oversight for the Market Network Manager, Market Growth Manager, and Market Clinical Manager, in coordination with respective corporate functional leaders
Strategically support all external market development activities led by Market Growth Manager and Market Network Manager, such as guiding payor, provider, and community partnerships
Works in a dyad relationship with the Market Medical Director to ensure ArchWell Health is delivering on the patient promise and meeting market performance objectives
Oversee network operations, ensuring a high-performance network is established and referrals are systematically & seamlessly coordinated for ArchWell Health patients

Deep focus on patient experience; gather appropriate team and patient information to build best-in-class customer service experience that optimizing resources for growth
Reviews financial reports to measure productivity and goal achievement and to determine areas needing cost reduction and improvement

Required Skills/Abilities:

Exposure to value-based models of care delivery; demonstrates a strong knowledge of the national payer and risk-bearing provider landscape

Strong business acumen; demonstrated experience in strategic planning, resource allocation, human resource modeling, leadership technique, and operations
Track record of developing and implementing processes for providing excellent customer service
Ability to effectively leverage business and organizational knowledge within and across functional areas
Must possess a high degree of emotional intelligence and integrity; driven and focused work ethic
Self-starter with the ability to think creatively and work effectively

Ability and willingness to travel locally, regionally and nationwide up to 50% of the time

Education and Experience:

Undergraduate degree in Business, Healthcare or Public Administration, Finance, Economics or a related field
Minimum of 7 years in a supervisory role in a medical or hospitality setting, with at least 2 years of multi-site experience

Experience managing and overseeing a multi-million dollar P&L highly desired
A passion for mentorship and team-development, particularly across multiple functional areas
A problem-solving orientation and eagerness to identify process gaps and implement practical solutions in a matrixed organization
Ability to manage multiple priorities across various stakeholders and departments
Embodies and serves as a role model of ArchWell Health’s Values:

Be compassionate
Strive for excellence
Earn trust
Show respect
Remain resilient

Do the right thing and do it with passion

title: Regional Growth Director
description:
ArchWell Health is a new, innovative healthcare provider devoted to improving the lives of our senior members. Our members experience greater continuity of care, as well as the comfort of knowing they will be treated with respect by people who genuinely care about them, their families, and their communities.

Job Summary:
Regional Growth Director (RGDs) are important leaders at ArchWell Health and are responsible for the teams that grow our patient base in the communities we serve. RGDs build and manage multiple Market Growth Teams across regional geographies. The Market Growth Teams are comprised of a Market Growth Manager, who leads a team of Membership Consultants and Community Relations Specialists, whose goal is to grow ArchWell Health’s patient membership base across multiple centers within a particular market.
The RGD reports directly to the Vice President of Growth & Marketing and will develop and execute a strategy to achieve intended patient membership targets for each market overseen. The RGD will report out regularly to the Executive Leadership Team on progress and activities transpiring in the local markets. For expansion markets, the RGD will be responsible for the staffing and development of the local Market Growth Teams. The RGD will assume the lead in managing the relationships with the local level sales leadership at the Medicare Advantage plans with which ArchWell Health is contracted as well as build and manage relationships with local FMOs and Independent Medicare Sales Agents. For existing markets, the RGD will ensure that all markets are fully-staffed and trained. The RGD will ensure the Market Growth Teams adhere to all compliance rules and will also manage the marketing budget for each of the markets. Prior management experience in Medicare Advantage sales or working with seniors is preferred though not required; we are a new breed of healthcare provider open to great sales leadership from many walks of life.

Developing productive relationships with local leaders of Medicare Advantage plans, FMOs/independent brokers, and community organizations
Leading the execution of market outreach and marketing initiatives
Advocating for your markets, teams, and members and reporting regularly to the Executive Leadership Team
Being an ambassador in the local communities by living the ArchWell Health values - building relationships with other healthcare providers, social/ community organizations, and marketing partners

Education and Experience:

Undergraduate degree preferred
Minimum of 4+ years of sales experience, preferably with a Medicare Advantage plan, FMO/benefits broker, or provider
5+ years of management experience
Experience working with seniors or the medically underserved preferred
A passion for mentorship and team-development, particularly across multiple functional areas
A valid Driver's License is required

title: Director of Development, Basic & Biomedical Sciences
description:
Job Function Summary:

Involves designing, developing, delivering, and administering fundraising programs. Identifies new donor prospects through researching background information on potential donors and developing materials, marketing plans, and organizing related programs / events; cultivates, stewards, and may solicit donor prospects.

Generic Scope

Recognized organization-wide expert. Has significant impact and influence on organizational policy and program development. Regularly leads projects of critical importance to the organization; these projects carry substantial consequences of success or failure. Directs programs with organization-wide impact (or may have impact beyond the University) that include formulating strategies and administering policies, processes, and resources. Significant barriers to entry exist at this level.

Custom Scope

Position Overview

Are you driven by the opportunity to power discoveries that transform human health on a global scale?

The Basic and Biomedical Sciences Development team is seeking an extraordinary, strategic, and collaborative Director of Development to advance philanthropic support for world-changing scientific innovation. Partnering directly with university deans, department chairs, institute directors, and world-renowned faculty, you will shape the future of medicine by securing major and principal gifts that accelerate breakthrough research and empower the next generation of scientific leaders.

This role offers an exceptional platform for an ambitious fundraising leader: a high-impact, broad-scope portfolio spanning foundational basic science departments, cutting-edge interdisciplinary research centers, the Division of Graduate Education and Postdoctoral Affairs (GEPA), and the prestigious Sandler Program for Breakthrough Biomedical Research (PBBR).

Why This Role Is Unique

  • Unrivaled Portfolio Breadth: Rather than working in a single niche, you will drive philanthropic strategies across an expansive ecosystem of basic sciences, multidisciplinary institutes, and graduate education.

  • Direct Access to Academic Leadership: You will serve as a trusted advisor to deans, department chairs, and pioneering researchers, translating complex scientific visions into inspiring donor opportunities.

  • High-Impact Philanthropy: Your work will directly fund high-risk, high-reward research (through PBBR) and nurture top-tier emerging scientists (through GEPA), leaving a lasting legacy on global health outcomes.

  • Collaborative Environment: Join a high-performing, deeply supportive team environment built on partnership, intellectual curiosity, and shared impact.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Portfolio & Prospect Management

  • Manage a dynamic portfolio of 75-100 major and principal gift prospects, actively moving donors through the pipeline from identification and qualification to solicitation and stewardship.

  • Target, cultivate, and solicit individual donors, foundations, and family offices capable of making gifts of $250k to $1M+.

Academic Partnership & Leadership Engagement

  • Work directly with deans, department chairs, center and institute directors, and faculty leaders to understand strategic research priorities and convert them into compelling philanthropic proposals.

  • Educate and coach faculty on fundraising best practices, serving as an expert partner in donor meetings and site visits.

Interdisciplinary Strategy & Programmatic Growth

  • Develop customized philanthropic strategies that leverage the strengths of interdisciplinary initiatives, basic science departments, GEPA, and PBBR.

  • Design and execute innovative proposals that connect donor passions with institution-wide scientific breakthroughs.

Desired Mindset & Competencies

  • Intellectual Curiosity: A genuine passion for basic science, scientific innovation, and medical research.

  • Strategic Agility: Comfort navigating complex institutional structures and managing multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously.

  • Collaborative Spirit: A team-first mindset with high emotional intelligence and a commitment to shared goals.

% of timeEssential Function (Yes/No)Key Responsibilities (To be completed by Supervisor)

40%

Yes

Serves as an expert or lead development professional in a specialized area such as major / principal gifts, gift planning or corporate / foundation relations, or a specific academic discipline that includes, or potentially includes, donors capable of making very significant contributions to the campus and / or medical center.

Portfolio Management

Core Objective: Directly manage and steward a dynamic portfolio of major and principal gift prospects (with capacity of $250k - $1M+), cultivating strategic donor relationships to advance transformative discovery and scientific innovation across basic science departments, research centers, GEPA, and PBBR.

  • Discovery & Innovation Solicitations: Lead face-to-face and virtual solicitations for major and principal commitments, matching donor vision with high-impact institutional priorities - including high-risk/high-reward seed research (PBBR), faculty recruitment, state-of-the-art instrumentation, and graduate student/postdoctoral fellowships (GEPA).
  • Complex Moves Management: Design and execute multi-stage cultivation and solicitation plans for high-net-worth individuals, tech/biotech entrepreneurs, and science-focused philanthropists, strategically moving donors from initial interest to multi-year investments in foundational science.
  • High-Touch Scientific Stewardship: Deliver customized stewardship - including private lab visits, intimate briefings with principal investigators (PIs), research impact updates, and exclusive symposia - demonstrating how donor investments accelerate groundbreaking discoveries and support the next generation of scientific leaders.
  • Portfolio Health & Velocity: Continuously evaluate portfolio performance based on contact quality, proposal conversion, and progress toward major gift revenue targets, actively prioritizing high-capacity prospects while maintaining strong pipeline momentum.

25%

Yes

Develops, creates, writes, implements, and / or evaluates individualized marketing plans and / or strategies for cultivation and solicitation of major gifts, gift planning or corporate / foundation prospects (strategies typically require a high degree of innovation).

Pipeline Development

Core Objective: Systematically identify, research, and qualify prospective major and principal gift donors by building strong, collaborative partnerships with department chairs, institute directors, GEPA leadership, and faculty researchers.

  • Faculty & Institutional Leadership Alignment: Partner closely with basic science department chairs, center and institute directors, PBBR leadership, and academic leaders to build trust, articulate funding priorities, and uncover high-potential philanthropic opportunities.
  • Proactive Prospecting & Network Expansion: Identify and cultivate high-capacity prospects across technology, biotechnology, venture capital, and entrepreneurial networks who possess an affinity for disruptive, data-driven, or exploratory biomedical research.
  • Venture & Advisory Board Engagement: Collaborate with volunteer leaders, scientific advisory boards, and institute advocates to leverage their personal and professional networks for warm, high-level introductions to prospective major donors.
  • Intelligence & CRM Discipline: Partner with the prospect research team to analyze wealth indicators, patent filings, corporate exits, and foundation giving trends, maintaining meticulous CRM strategy tracking for all science and graduate education prospects.

15%

Yes

Writes complex proposals for solicitation of high value individuals, corporate, and / or foundation prospects.

Prospect Strategy & Proposal Writing

Core Objective: Develop bespoke cultivation strategies and author sophisticated, highly tailored major gift proposals that translate complex fundamental research into inspiring philanthropic opportunities.

  • Bespoke Proposal & Case Writing: Author compelling, impact-driven major gift proposals, white papers, letters of intent, and pledge agreements that clearly articulate the transformative potential of basic research, multidisciplinary initiatives, and trainee support.
  • Complex & Structured Giving: Collaborate with planned giving specialists, tax advisors, and family office representatives to structure complex gifts, including seed funding models, endowed chairs, graduate fellowships, and blended gift commitments.
  • Institutional Priority Translation: Work directly with faculty, PIs, and academic leadership to translate technical, cutting-edge biomedical concepts (e.g., genetics, cell biology, neuroscience, immunology) into accessible, visionary donor proposals.
  • Individualized Strategy Roadmaps: Formulate multi-year engagement strategies for top-tier individual prospects, aligning donor interests with institutional strengths across basic science departments and campus-wide initiatives like PBBR.

15%

YES

Analyzes needs and creates strategic and long-range plans for fundraising and other advancement programs and may have the authority to make commitments and precedent-setting decisions regarding program design, development, and procedures.

Leadership & Stakeholder Alignment

Core Objective: Engage executive leadership, department heads, and faculty partners to elevate high-stakes major gift opportunities and foster a collaborative advancement culture.

  • Faculty Coaching & Strategy Prep: Brief and coach department chairs, institute directors, and research faculty prior to donor interactions, providing detailed meeting briefs, messaging frameworks, and explicit roles for joint solicitations.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner seamlessly with advancement and university colleagues to ensure unified donor messaging and compliant gift execution.
  • Advancement Collaboration across GEPA & PBBR: Serve as a subject-matter resource and strategic liaison for interdisciplinary initiatives bridging basic science departments, postdoctoral affairs, and campus-wide research programs.
  • Exclusive Donor Engagements: Conceptualize and host intimate donor gatherings, salon dinners, and executive briefings featuring leading researchers to build community and advance principal gift relationships.

5%

YES

Other Duties as Assigned

Core Objective: Maintain flexibility to support broader institutional advancement priorities, special projects, and team-wide campaigns.

  • Special Campaigns & Institutional Initiatives: Support priority campaigns, institutional milestones, or emergency research funding initiatives as directed by advancement leadership.
  • Departmental & Team Support: Participate in team planning, staff mentoring, and cross-departmental working groups to enhance advancement processes, templates, and collaborative workflows.

Knowledge, Skills and AbilitiesReq / Pref
Expert working knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations concepts, principles, procedures, and techniques.Req
Expert knowledge of all aspects of the institution, campus or medical center, including current issues of concern for both the campus and / or throughout higher education / healthcare, generally. Expert knowledge of the location, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure.Pref

Expert written and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the organization and with outside constituencies. Expert skills in making persuasive and compelling presentations of goals and objectives for a location in order to secure gifts.Req
Expert organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills. Expert project / program management skills, including skills in setting and meeting program / project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.Req
Expert level skills in maintaining confidentiality.Req
Bachelor's degree in related area and 10+ years of related expeirence / or equivalent experience / training.Req

title: Dairy Supervisor
description:
Why choose us?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.


Position Summary

The Dairy Supervisor provides leadership and direction for the daily operation of the Dairy Department. This position helps ensure dairy products are properly stocked, rotated, merchandised, and maintained at appropriate temperatures while supporting excellent customer service, inventory control, shrink reduction, cleanliness, and food safety standards.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide leadership and direction to Dairy Department associates.
  • Ensure dairy shelves, coolers, and displays remain fully stocked, organized, clean, and visually appealing.
  • Stock and replenish milk, eggs, cheese, yogurt, refrigerated beverages, and other dairy products as needed.
  • Monitor inventory levels and assist with ordering to maintain appropriate product quantities.
  • Receive, organize, and properly store incoming dairy merchandise.
  • Follow proper product rotation procedures and regularly check expiration and sell-by dates.
  • Monitor product freshness and quality and promptly remove damaged, expired, or unsellable merchandise.
  • Maintain proper cold-chain procedures and ensure refrigerated products are stored at appropriate temperatures.
  • Assist with inventory management and help identify opportunities to reduce shrink, damages, and product loss.
  • Maintain organized backstock and ensure products are easily accessible for efficient replenishment.
  • Ensure promotional and advertised products are properly stocked, displayed, and signed.
  • Maintain accurate pricing, shelf tags, and product placement throughout the department.
  • Build and maintain displays according to merchandising standards and promotional plans.
  • Monitor department conditions throughout the shift and respond to low-stock items and operational needs.
  • Maintain clean and organized dairy coolers, shelves, cases, storage areas, and workspaces.
  • Follow all food safety, sanitation, health, and workplace safety requirements.
  • Ensure associates safely use department equipment and follow proper product-handling procedures.
  • Communicate inventory concerns, out-of-stocks, equipment issues, staffing needs, and other operational concerns to store leadership.
  • Assist with opening and closing responsibilities as assigned.
  • Support other departments and store operations as needed.
Leadership Expectations
  • Lead by example and maintain a professional, positive, and productive work environment.
  • Provide associates with clear assignments, expectations, and appropriate follow-up.
  • Train and coach associates on stocking, rotation, merchandising, food safety, and department standards.
  • Monitor associate productivity and ensure assigned responsibilities are completed accurately and efficiently.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, urgency, and excellent customer service.
  • Maintain a visible presence in the department and respond quickly to customer and associate needs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve product availability, department organization, merchandising, and shrink.
  • Maintain consistent communication with store leadership regarding department performance and operational needs.
  • Help ensure the department is clean, stocked, organized, and customer-ready throughout the day.
Qualifications
  • Previous retail, grocery, dairy, stocking, or related experience preferred.
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of dairy products, stocking, rotation, merchandising, and inventory practices preferred.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to provide direction and support to associates.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.
  • Must be dependable, organized, professional, and able to demonstrate good judgment.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule based on business needs, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Ability to bend, reach, squat, kneel, push, pull, and perform repetitive motions.
  • Ability to regularly lift and move dairy products, milk crates, cases, boxes, and department supplies as required.
  • Ability to push and maneuver stocking carts and other department equipment.
  • Ability to work for extended periods in refrigerated and cooler environments.
  • Ability to safely operate stocking and department equipment after receiving appropriate training.

title: Benefit Programs Specialist I
description:

title: SW Optimization Engineer AI/ML
description:
At Apple, our Platform Architecture group is responsible for connecting our hardware and software into one unified system. You’ll collaborate with engineers across Apple to design how all of our technologies work in unison, drive development of our renowned system-on-a-chip (SoC) architecture, and develop forward-looking prototype systems and software. Our team is driving performance enhancements in application and system software and developing novel algorithms to deliver integrated, highly optimized solutions based on Apple Silicon.

In this role, you will analyze existing and new workloads to identify performance bottlenecks in the hardware and/or software. Working with your colleagues, you'll address performance limitations and provide recommendations for Apple hardware and software improvements. In addition to working directly with developers, you will identify patterns of performance challenges on Apple silicon, emerging new usage models, and provide feedback to the silicon and software teams for potential improvements.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent job-related experience in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Experience in software development for at least one of the following hardware IPs: AI/ML HW accelerators, GPUs processing units, image/video encoders, or similar.
  • Experience with AI/ML, graphics, or HPC performance benchmarks and workloads.

Preferred Qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field.
  • 10+ years of relevant experience in software performance optimization, performance analysis tools, performance optimization process and development of efficient computational algorithms.
  • Knowledge of computer architecture fundamentals.
  • Proficiency in some of the C/C++ family programming languages, and scripting languages such as Python.
  • Ability to prototype and benchmark algorithms on CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine platforms, analyze performance metrics, and create high-level complexity models, or develop targeted highly efficient low-level performance libraries for AI/ML accelerators or GPUs.
  • Proficiency in popular AI/ML frameworks, such as PyTorch, and relevant software stacks.
  • Knowledge of operating system internals and compiler technologies.
  • Technical aptitude and curiosity, as well as ability to collaborate effectively with team members, partners, and stakeholders.

title: Software & Integrations Developer (CRM)
description:
Position: Software & Integrations Developer (CRM)Location: Vaudreuil, Quebec
Work model: Hybrid, with a minimum of two full days per week in our Vaudreuil officeStatus: Full-time, permanent (1) (This is a newly created position within the organization)

Build the CRM platform behind a growing North American business

At Quadra, Salesforce is not a side system. It is how our commercial teams find, win, and serve customers across North America. We are looking for a Software & Integrations Developer (CRM) to build, extend, and integrate that platform as the business grows.

Reporting to the Commercial Applications Manager, you will be hands-on with Apex, Flows, Lightning, integrations, and releases. You will work closely with the business, the data, and the people who use the platform every day.

This role is ideal for a developer who enjoys ownership: ownership of a build, a release, and a result. You'll join a company that is small enough for your work to be visible, yet large enough for it to have a meaningful impact.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.
For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years, and as one of the Best Workplaces in Canada® in 2025. A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!
Why This Role Matters

You will build and extend the platform our commercial teams run on — Sales Cloud, Experience Cloud, Account Engagement and the integration behind them.
You will own real development work end to end: design, build, test, deploy and support, with source control and CI/CD as the standard, not the exception.
You will connect Salesforce to the rest of the business — ERP, transportation and marketing — through MuleSoft and APIs.
You will work directly with sales, customer service and marketing teams, close enough to the business to challenge a requirement before you build it.
You will help bring AI and automation into day-to-day commercial work, including Agentforce, Flows and agent-based solutions.

What will be your main responsibilities as a Software & Integrations Developer (CRM)?

Lead the configuration and customization of Salesforce using Apex, Lightning Components, Visualforce, Flows and platform automation.
Design and implement integrations between Salesforce and other Quadra systems using MuleSoft and APIs, ensuring reliable and scalable data flows across CRM, ERP and marketing platforms.
Champion and apply source control (Git) and CI/CD best practices to support development, deployments and release management across environments.
Provide expert oversight of Salesforce configuration, including users, profiles, roles, permissions, sharing rules, custom objects, fields and validation rules.
Develop and optimize reports, dashboards and flows that support commercial operations and business decision-making.
Ensure the integrity, quality and governance of enterprise data across the CRM ecosystem.
Assess platform readiness and lead release preparedness activities for Salesforce seasonal releases, upgrades and system enhancements.
Translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions, while challenging assumptions and identifying opportunities to simplify and optimize outcomes.
Contribute technical expertise to project planning, effort estimation and delivery commitments.
Collaborate with developers, administrators, Product Owners and technology partners to drive cohesive and effective solution delivery.
Communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Identify, recommend and implement platform improvements, while maintaining expertise in Salesforce capabilities, emerging technologies and industry best practices.

What are the required qualifications to have success in this position?

5+ years of proven Salesforce development experience, with a solid understanding of Salesforce architecture and best practices.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology or a relevant technology-focused discipline, or equivalent experience.
Proficiency in Apex, Visualforce and Lightning Components.
Hands-on experience with Sales Cloud is required; Experience Cloud and Account Engagement (Pardot) are an asset.
Experience with integration tools, APIs and third-party applications; MuleSoft experience is an asset.
Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer, MuleSoft Developer, Platform App Builder, Account Engagement (Pardot) Specialist, Agentforce Specialist) are highly preferred.
Working knowledge of source control (Git) and CI/CD practices in a Salesforce context.
Knowledge of adjacent commercial applications such as ERP or marketing automation platforms is an asset.
Previous experience working in a SCRUM or agile environment is an asset.
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.
Strong communication and collaboration skills; bilingualism (French and English) is preferred for this position.

Working Conditions:

Permanent, full-time position based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, Quebec.
Hybrid model: mandatory presence in the Vaudreuil office a minimum of 2 full days per week, in line with Quadra policy.
Occasional travel to collaborate with Quadra sites, vendors or external partners within Canada and the United States.
Occasional off-hours involvement during major releases or critical business events.
Requires autonomy, strong collaboration and comfort working across both business and technology topics.

You Might Be the Right Person If…
You like owning a build from the first conversation to the release note. You are the developer people trust with production, because your work is tested, documented and in source control. You ask what problem we are actually solving before you start building, and you push back when a request adds complexity without adding value. You are pragmatic: you build what fits a 650-person company, not a 10,000-person one. And you care as much about whether the business actually uses what you shipped as about how elegantly it was built.
We want to meet you!
Here are some of the perks of choosing Quadra:

Permanent, full-time position: Join us for a stable, long-term career
Competitive salary & Performance Incentives: Your hard work is rewarded with attractive compensation and bonuses

Hybrid Work & Autonomy: A hybrid schedule and the autonomy to manage your own time!

Tailored training: We provide personalized training to support you and your growth
Excellent Benefits Package: Medical, Dental, HSA, and more to keep you covered including our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and access to telemedicine/Virtual healthcare
Generous Time Off: Flexible personal days, sick days and vacation to recharge
Wellness Programs: Enhance your quality of life with wellness initiatives, including health and mental wellness programs from healthcare leaders
Pension plan with match: Plan your future with our matched pension plan program
Tech Perks: We got you covered with cellphone and internet costs
Family-owned and support environment: Be part of a private, family-owned company with a strong infrastructure and core values
Award-Winning Workplace: Work in a certified Great Place to Work®, and Best Managed Company!
Inclusive Culture: We celebrate diversity and caring for each other and having fun are part of our core values!
Career Growth: Unlock opportunities for development in a fast-paced growing company
Fun Social Activities: Get involved in company events, Volunteering programs, etc.
Referral & Recognition Programs: Earn monetary rewards through our referral and employee recognition programs (years of service, merit awards, etc.)
And Much More !

Please note that this base salary range is provided for reference purposes only. Individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.
Base salary represents just one component of our overall compensation package. This role is also eligible for a generous incentive program and comprehensive benefits. title: Technical Business Analyst
description:
Role Overview

Loggerhead’s IT team is seeking a Technical Business Analyst to bridge business needs, customer experience, and technical delivery. This role partners with business stakeholders, product owners, UX/UI designers, solution engineers, developers, quality assurance teams, and external vendors to define effective technology solutions. The ideal candidate can lead to functional requirements analysis across user interfaces, workflows, business rules, data, systems, and integrations while also interpreting API specifications and documenting the requirements used to design new or updated APIs.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role requires strong functional analysis, technical aptitude, user-centered thinking, precise documentation, sound judgment, and clear communication. The Technical Business Analyst must be comfortable moving between customer and business needs, UI/UX workflows, and detailed system and integration requirements while identifying gaps, dependencies, and opportunities for improvement.


Key Responsibilities

  • Business and Functional Analysis: Elicit, analyze, validate, and document business, functional, nonfunctional, data, UI/UX, system, and integration requirements.
  • Translate business goals, customer needs, workflows, and data needs into clear requirements, user stories, use cases, acceptance criteria, process maps, data maps, and other delivery artifacts.
  • Facilitate discovery sessions, stakeholder interviews, workflow reviews, and solution-design discussions to understand current-state challenges and define future-state experiences.
  • Document business rules, system behavior, screen requirements, field definitions, validations, user interactions, permissions, notifications, and exception scenarios.
  • Ensure requirements are complete, approved, traceable, testable, and maintained throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Identify requirement gaps, assumptions, dependencies, risks, and conflicting stakeholder needs, and drive timely resolution.
  • UI/UX and Customer Experience: Partner with business stakeholders, designers, developers, and QA teams to define intuitive, accessible, and consistent user experiences.
  • Create or contribute to user flows, journey maps, wireframes, screen annotations, prototypes, and functional specifications for customer-facing and internal applications.
  • Evaluate proposed designs against business objectives, user needs, functional requirements, usability principles, accessibility expectations, and technical constraints.
  • Define interface behavior for navigation, data entry, validation, messaging, errors, responsive layouts, and alternate user paths.
  • Participate in design reviews and usability feedback sessions, document decisions, and ensure approved experiences are accurately translated into development requirements.
  • API and Integration Analysis: Review and interpret REST API specifications, including endpoints, HTTP methods, request and response payloads, authentication, headers, status codes, validation rules, error handling, and data definitions.
  • Document the business and technical requirements used by solution engineers and developers to design new or updated APIs.
  • Create source-to-target data mappings, field-level definitions, transformation rules, required and optional field requirements, business rules, and integration acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with developers and solution engineers to define API contracts and confirm that proposed specifications support the intended business process, user experience, and system behavior.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and dependencies in existing API documentation and coordinate decisions with business stakeholders, technical teams, and vendors.
  • Use Swagger/OpenAPI documentation and Postman to evaluate integrations, build requests, inspect payloads and responses, and validate expected API behavior.
  • Product and Delivery Support: Develop strong product, platform, customer journey, and system knowledge to support solution design and continuous improvement.
  • Support Agile ceremonies, backlog refinement, release planning, and the creation of epics, features, user stories, tasks, and acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with product, design, development, and quality assurance teams to clarify requirements and support delivery throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Testing and Validation: Define functional, usability, integration, negative, regression, and end-to-end test scenarios based on documented requirements.
  • Support user acceptance testing by validating workflows, screen behavior, business rules, data, permissions, messaging, usability, and expected outcomes.
  • Support API testing by validating authentication, headers, payloads, responses, status codes, error conditions, data transformations, and downstream outcomes.
  • Document defects and requirement variances, support root-cause analysis, and confirm that delivered solutions meet approved functional, user experience, and technical requirements.
  • Documentation, Training, and Collaboration: Create and maintain business requirements documents, functional specifications, process flows, workflow diagrams, data dictionaries, integration documentation, decision logs, and user guidance.
  • Facilitate cross-functional discussions, communicate technical concepts clearly to business audiences, and ensure business and user context is accurately conveyed to technical teams.
  • Create and deliver training materials when needed to support successful adoption of new systems, integrations, and processes.
  • Use tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub, Asana, Visio, Power BI, Microsoft 365, Postman, and Swagger/OpenAPI to manage requirements, collaboration, analysis, and delivery.
  • Take on additional responsibilities as needed to support team and business priorities.


Required Qualifications

  • Five or more years of experience as a Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, Technical Business Analyst, or similar role supporting software development, user-facing applications, and systems integration.
  • Demonstrated experience eliciting and documenting business, functional, nonfunctional, UI/UX, data, system, and integration requirements.
  • Experience translating business processes and user needs into user stories, use cases, process flows, wireframes, functional specifications, business rules, and testable acceptance criteria.
  • Experience partnering with product owners, designers, developers, and QA teams to define and deliver customer-facing or internal user experiences.
  • Working knowledge of user-centered design, usability, accessibility, responsive design, and common interface patterns.
  • Demonstrated experience interpreting REST API specifications and translating integration needs into detailed requirements used by development teams to design new or updated APIs.
  • Experience documenting API endpoints, request and response payloads, field definitions, source-to-target mappings, authentication, validation rules, error responses, business rules, and acceptance criteria.
  • Working knowledge of JSON, RESTful services, HTTP methods, status codes, API authentication methods, and integration patterns.
  • Hands-on experience using Postman and Swagger/OpenAPI documentation to understand, validate, and document API behavior.
  • Proven ability to analyze and communicate complex business processes, customer journeys, system behavior, and technical requirements.
  • Strong understanding of Agile delivery, product development, testing practices, and the software development lifecycle.
  • Ability to facilitate cross-functional discussions, resolve ambiguities, and drive alignment among business stakeholders, vendors, designers, and technical teams.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to business audiences and preserve business and user context for technical teams.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities and requirements.
  • Experience working with cloud-based applications, integrations, and delivery teams.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in the Property and Casualty insurance industry, including policy, billing, claims, quoting, or CRM platforms.
  • Experience with XML, OAuth, webhooks, event-driven integrations, or other common integration technologies and patterns.
  • Experience writing or interpreting relational and non-relational queries and using data analysis to validate requirements and outcomes.
  • Experience with observability or troubleshooting tools such as Datadog.
  • Experience with prototyping or design collaboration tools such as Figma or similar platforms.
  • Experience creating reports, spreadsheets, dashboards, and executive-ready analysis.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and a customer-focused mindset.


Education & Certifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, information technology, computer science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Business analysis, Agile, product management, or project management certification is preferred.


Working Conditions

  • This is a hybrid position that requires a minimum of two days per week at our corporate headquarters.
  • Flexible hours and occasional weekend availability may be required.
  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work permanently in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. The role

We are hiring a Monitoring Officer (12-month term) and a Senior Finance Officer (15-month term) to support the Finance and Procurement Services Branch. Ideal candidates will demonstrate our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.

Monitoring Officer - 12-month term (Bilingual Imperative BBB/BBB)

Do you have keen problem-solving skills? Can you provide strong advice and guidance in a financial control environment? Do you have a proven record of making professionally sound decisions and judgments to provide advice, direction and recommendations to management regarding financial processes? Then you are the candidate we are looking for.

The Financial Monitoring team is looking for a Monitoring Officer who will be responsible for reviewing key financial processes and internal controls to ensure that their design are appropriate and that internal controls are working as intended. Duties include planning and executing or coordinating monitoring activities through statistical sampling, data mining, data analytics or data base query mechanisms, to ensure that business processes such as accounts payable, credit card purchases, transfer payments, revenue collections, asset acquisitions and assets under construction are processed in compliance with policies and procedures and that proper internal controls are in place. Additionally, the Monitoring Officer can lead special projects to review, evaluate and investigate the effectiveness and efficiencies of internal control, financial management and compliance with existing policies, systems, procedures and practices.

Senior Finance Officer, Accounting Operations - 15-month term (Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC)

In addition, the Accounts Payable team is looking for a Senior Finance Officer who will be responsible for account verification framework and reporting for the oversight committee in addition to other tasks including supervision and Section 33 approvals for payments, interdepartmental settlements and payroll. title: DC LIFT TRUCK OPERATOR - 3rd Shift
description:
DC Lift Truck Operator

About Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc.

At SBH, our purpose is to inspire a more colorful, confident, and welcoming world. We are the leader in professional hair color, selling and distributing professional beauty supplies across 11 countries through our Sally Beauty and Beauty Systems Group businesses. Sally Beauty offers products for hair color, hair care, nails, and skin care to retail customers looking for salon quality products at a value price. Beauty Systems Group, branded as Cosmo Prof or Armstrong McCall stores, along with its direct sales consultants, sell professionally branded products intended for use and resale by salons to retail consumers.

About the role

This job consists of operating manual and/or Power Industrial equipment to complete the process of at least one of the following: receiving, picking, packing, stocking, or shipping of products. Primary goal is to move product safely while maximizing productivity. Detailed Standard Operating Procedures exist for tasks performed by this job in the following areas: Receiving, Order Pulling, Shipping and Stocking. Attributes: Breakdown, CasePuller, Cycle Counting, Ecom Full Service, Ecomindirect, Happy Beauty Co. Key In, Loading, Put Away Reach, Put Away TSP, Put Away Man Up, Restocking, Returns, Special Projects, Unloader, Inv Cont, Cardboard, Quick Ship, Batching

Responsibilities

  • May complete the activity of RF Scanners or paper-based picking which requires the use of different types of powered industrial powered equipment to complete this process and includes the obtaining and transferring product from various locations throughout the DC,

Shipping Product:

  • May complete the activity of shipping which requires the use of different types of equipment to complete this process and will include the weighing, loading/stacking of materials onto trucks

Receiving Products:

  • May complete the activity of receiving in products from various vendors which will require the use of different types of equipment to complete the process and will include the unloading, stacking, and storage of product during and after the receiving process.

Stock Products:

  • May stock products/items which require the use of different types of equipment to complete the process and will include obtaining and transferring product from various locations throughout the distribution center, along with pick up from the receiving staging area.
  • Maintains a safe work environment, performs job functions in a safe manner, and reports any potential job hazards and property damage to leadership, including maintaining good housekeeping practices.
  • Maintains productivity related to standards based on assigned task.
  • Performs other duties as assigned or requested by leadership.

Knowledge, skills & abilities requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Experience preferred in a distribution/warehouse environment or equivalent work experience including the operation of heavy equipment
  • Basic computer skills
  • Verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with the capability to adjust to change and interruptions
  • Ability to work with limited supervision
  • Must be able to become certified through the Sally Beauty Lift Truck Training Program in order to efficiently and safely operate a forklift within the time frame specified by Leadership

Competencies & attributes

  • Passionate Learner actively learns; asks questions to gain further understanding; open to feedback; applies leaning to role; considers learning important and completes when assigned
  • Flexible & Agile Adapter open to change, works well with little direction and finishes the task, keeps calm under pressure and doesn't dwell on the past
  • Talent Builder shares knowledge with others, considers how to include others to problem solve and gain knowledge, looks for ways to acknowledge and motivate others
  • Effective Communicator can articulate well when sharing information, self-aware of impact and style when communicating to engage others, asks questions and listens
  • Team Builder works well with others, collaborates with a wide number of associates/teams, acts humbly when a part of a team and understands the importance of including others
  • Customer Focused Partner understands the customer and shares insights, values the customer and eager to make a positive impact, holds self to a good standard of customer service
  • Strategic Thinker brings new, strategic ideas to the team, actively supports strategic plans, provides additional ideas to drive improvements
  • Big Picture Thinker understands how the team operates, knows how decisions could impact other teams
  • Results Driver holds self to a good standard of work and delivery, manages own time and focuses on the right priorities, self-motivated, adapts easily, demonstrates grit

Problem Solver & Decision Maker uses the right information to make decisions and take action with others to solve problems, uses good judgement to make prompt yet balanced decisions

Working conditions & physical requirements

The work environment involves everyday risks or discomforts associated with working in a warehouse environment, which requires heightened safety precautions typical of loading/receiving docks and high-volume inventory management operations, e.g., use of safe work practices with light to heavy equipment, while utilizing forklifts and pallet jacks, avoidance of trips and falls, observance of fire regulations, etc. Exposure to occasional fumes and odors and/or temperature fluctuations (25 degrees to 105 degrees Fahrenheit) is possible.

The position requires some physical exertion and the able to perform the basic lifting and system tasks for all warehouse functions and departments including receiving, put away, picking, packing, cycle counting, order checking and shipping. The work requires the repetitively lifting of cartons weighing 10 to 55 pounds, standing/walking for 6 to 10 hours a day, and climbing up and down stairs and ladders.

title: Subsidiary Controller
description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Subsidiary Controller is the senior financial leader for Colonial Chemical Solutions and is responsible for overseeing all accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, and financial analysis activities for the business. This position serves as a strategic business partner to subsidiary leadership and works closely with operations, sales, supply chain, and corporate management to improve profitability, optimize working capital, support growth initiatives, and ensure compliance with company policies and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
The Subsidiary Controller is accountable for the integrity of the subsidiary's financial information and provides financial leadership to support operational and strategic decision-making.
DUTIES & RESPNSIBILITIES
Financial Leadership and Reporting

Direct and oversee all accounting activities for the subsidiary, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting.
Coordinate and manage monthly, quarterly, and annual closing processes.
Review financial statements, operating results, and key performance indicators for accuracy, reasonableness, and consistency.
Analyze financial performance and communicate results, trends, risks, and opportunities to subsidiary and corporate leadership.
Ensure compliance with GAAP and company accounting policies.

Business Partnership and Performance Management

Partner with subsidiary leadership to develop and execute strategies that improve profitability, cash flow, and return on invested capital.
Provide financial guidance and decision support related to pricing, customer profitability, inventory management, capital expenditures, and growth initiatives.
Evaluate financial impacts of operational decisions and recommend actions to improve business performance.
Participate in strategic planning and long-term business initiatives.

Budgeting and Forecasting

Lead the annual budgeting process and periodic forecasting activities.
Develop financial models and business analyses to support management decision-making.
Monitor performance against budget and forecast and explain significant variances.
Identify key drivers of financial performance and recommend corrective actions when necessary.

Inventory and Operations Accounting

Oversee inventory accounting, valuation, reserves, and controls.
Monitor inventory levels, turnover, obsolescence, and working capital performance.
Partner with operations and supply chain leadership to improve inventory management and operational efficiency.
Analyze transportation, warehousing, packaging, and distribution costs and identify opportunities for improvement.

Internal Controls and Compliance

Maintain and strengthen internal controls, accounting procedures, and financial processes.
Ensure compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and audit standards.
Coordinate internal and external audit activities for the subsidiary.
Implement process improvements and system enhancements to increase efficiency and accuracy.

Cash Flow and Working Capital Management

Monitor subsidiary cash flow, accounts receivable, inventory, and accounts payable performance.
Develop strategies to improve working capital utilization and cash generation.
Support treasury and financing initiatives as required.

Leadership and Talent Development

Lead, supervise, and develop accounting and finance personnel within the subsidiary.
Establish performance expectations and provide coaching and professional development opportunities.
Foster collaboration among finance, operations, sales, supply chain, and other functional areas.
Promote a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer service.

Special Projects

Support acquisitions, integrations, system implementations, and strategic initiatives.
Perform special analyses and projects as requested by subsidiary or corporate leadership.
Perform other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
Seven to ten years of progressive accounting and financial management experience.
Previous Controller, Assistant Controller, Finance Director, or Corporate Controller experience.
Certified Public Accountant (CPA) preferred.

title: Quality Inspector II
description:
Quality Inspector II

About Nissha Medical Technologies

Nissha Medical Technologies (NMT) is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) where people, purpose, and technology come together to advance healthcare. Headquartered in the United States, NMT is the medical devices business unit and a wholly owned subsidiary of Nissha Co., Ltd., a publicly traded Japanese company based in Kyoto, Japan (TSE: 7915).

Across our global organization, our teams collaborate to design and manufacture innovative medical devices and solutions that make a real difference in patients’ lives. We partner closely with our customers to solve complex challenges, move ideas forward, and support products from concept through commercialization. Our work spans patient monitoring, surgical and interventional solutions, precision components, and emerging technologies, all grounded in a strong culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

At Nissha Medical Technologies, we believe our success is driven by our people. We foster an environment where curiosity is encouraged, teamwork is valued, and individuals are empowered to grow their skills and careers. If you’re motivated by meaningful work, collaboration, and the opportunity to help shape the future of healthcare, you’ll find a place to belong at NMT.

What You Will Do

The Quality Inspector II is responsible for verifying incoming raw materials, in-process, and final product to ensure that materials that do not conform to specification are prevented from being used or delivered. Maintains appropriate records to complete the evidence of conformance and performs the following essential functions and basic duties:

  • Follow Employee guidelines and Quality System Regulations as defined by Nissha Medical Technologies practices, policies and Standard Operating Procedures to ensure that customer requirements and industry standards and regulations are met.

  • Demonstrate knowledge and act in accordance with NMT’s Employee Guidelines and applicable quality standards as outlined in NMT’s Quality Manual.

  • Inspection of components and documentation for purchased product.

  • Inspect product using standard inspection gages such as micrometers and vernier/calipers, optical comparators, and visual coordinate measurement systems.

  • Inspection of product using visual standards.

  • Testing of product using tensile testing equipment.

  • Use of good documentation practices (GDP) of inspection results for presentation to Material Review Board and inspection history files.

  • Generate Quality Material Reports (QMR) to document discrepant materials.

  • Process dispositioned material after inspection and/or MRB activities.

  • Maintain accurate Inspection Record files.

  • Interact with all levels of company team members.

  • Perform In-Process and Final Inspections where applicable.

  • Gather sterilization and other external records for inclusion into the Device History Record (DHR).

  • Provide lot release documentation to customers as required.

  • Review and approve the final DHR packet authorizing release of product.

  • Assist with production re-inspection activities as needed.

  • Support internal/external audits by providing evidence as requested.

  • May be required to work overtime when necessary.

  • Other duties or special projects may be assigned as requested.

  • Abides by all safety and security rules set forth by the company and regulatory agencies

  • Regular attendance is required.

What You Bring

Core Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED)

  • Minimum 2 years of related experience, Medical Device preferred.

  • Demonstrated proficiency in MD Suite, particularly Microsoft (MS) Word and Excel.

  • Knowledge of GD&T and able to read and interpret drawings/specifications.

  • Familiarity with standard inspection tools to include calipers, micrometers, optical comparator, scales, and pin gauges.

  • Must be highly organized, detail oriented, and work effectively as both a team member and independent contributor.

  • Strong written and oral communication skills.

  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and Maintenance instructions and procedure manuals.

  • Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.

  • Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.

  • Well-developed verbal, numerical reasoning, and analysis skills with ability to draw sound conclusions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience designing fixtures or tooling is preferred

  • Vision System and CMM operation experience preferred.

  • ASQ CQI preferred.


Professional Traits We Value

  • Problem-solving ability
  • Works well in a collaborative team environment

Compensation & Benefits

The expected salary range for this position is $21.00 – $23.00/hour. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location.

In addition, Nissha Medical Technologies offers a competitive total rewards package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off, life and disability insurance, and professional development opportunities.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Nissha Medical Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants and do not discriminate based on any protected status under applicable law.

title: Organic Growth & Search Director
description:
About the role

Location: New York City (Hybrid). In-office at least three days per week (Tues, Wed, & Thurs)

Compensation: $230,000-$250,000 total cash compensation (base salary + variable) + equity + benefits (This range is reflective of level of contribution. Candidates who fully match what we’re looking for in this role will be at the top of the range.)

About the Role

Daloopa is looking for a Director of Organic Growth & Search to own how our brand and products are discovered across traditional and AI-powered search.


You will lead our strategy across SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and organic experimentation, with a focus on growing high-value, non-branded discovery and qualified pipeline.


You will also ensure Daloopa’s broader brand momentum—from PR, partnerships, brand activations and content—translates into lasting organic value through authoritative links, citations, and visibility.

What You’ll Do

  • Own organic growth: Develop and execute Daloopa’s strategy across SEO, AEO/GEO, and emerging organic channels, with a focus on driving non-branded discovery and pipeline.
  • Grow search visibility (including AI search): Own keyword strategy, on-page and technical SEO, internal linking, and site architecture. Establish how Daloopa shows up across AI-powered search and answer engines, and test strategies to increase relevant citations and visibility.
  • Shape organic content strategy: Identify priority search opportunities and partner with PMMs and subject-matter experts to optimize content for traditional and AI search.
  • Turn brand momentum into authority: Partner with brand, comms, and demand generation stakeholders to translate PR, brand activations, and campaigns into authoritative links, mentions, and citations.
  • Experiment and optimize: Build a disciplined testing program across content, landing pages, conversion paths, and traditional and AI search to identify and scale what drives qualified organic growth.
  • Measure business impact: Establish reporting across organic visibility, engagement and conversion, partnering with Marketing leadership and Marketing Ops / RevOps to continually improve attribution.

Who You Are

  • 8+ years of experience in SEO, search strategy, and/or organic growth, ideally at a B2B technology, fintech or SaaS company.
  • Deep expertise across SEO (including technical SEO), search intent, site architecture, and authority building.
  • Strong understanding of AI search and hands-on experience with AEO/GEO strategies and experimentation.
  • Track record of growing non-branded organic discovery and connecting organic programs to qualified leads, pipeline, or revenue.
  • Strategic but hands-on—you can set the roadmap while also digging into search data, auditing pages, and launching experiments.
  • Proficient with tools for search performance (Google Search Console), web analytics (GA4), SEO research (Semrush or Ahrefs), and AEO/GEO visibility (Profound, AthenaHQ, or similar).
  • Strong cross-functional partner.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with financial services, investment research, and/or workflows tools (API, MCP, LLMs).
  • Experience working in a startup or high-growth environment.

Success Looks Like

  • Daloopa materially expands its visibility for high-value, non-branded searches relevant to our target audience.
  • Daloopa becomes increasingly visible and cited across AI-powered search experiences, supported by a scalable AEO/GEO playbook across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.
  • Organic discovery becomes a growing source of qualified pipeline.
  • Daloopa has a repeatable experimentation engine for identifying and scaling new sources of organic growth.

Apply

If you enjoy combining deep search expertise with a growth mindset and are excited to build an organic growth engine we want to hear from you! Share an experience that shows how you moved the needle.
