title: Quality Technician
description:
Quality Technician

At Multi-Color Corporation (MCC), we're looking for a detail-focused Quality Technician who will support quality assurance across the value stream. You'll partner closely with the Quality Manager to help ensure products, processes, and documentation meet customer requirements and MCC quality standards while following defined procedures.

As the global leader in premium label solutions, MCC produces the labels found on many of the world's most recognized consumer brands. Our Bowling Green facility combines advanced manufacturing technology with a culture focused on safety, development, continuous improvement, and long-term career growth.

Our need is currently 2nd shift which inclues +$1.00 shift differential

Pay & Benefits

Paid Holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Day After Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, plus two floating holidays
Benefits: Competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, and 401(k)

Why This Role Is Different

This role gives you the opportunity to work directly with quality assurance activities that support products, processes, and documentation across the value stream.

You'll approve labels, processes, materials, and roll-end retains, maintain color tolerance and consistency files, analyze reject and quality data, and support the MCC Quality Management System. You'll also participate in internal audits, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality-related projects, giving you hands-on exposure to both day-to-day quality control and broader quality systems work.

This role offers the opportunity to strengthen your quality assurance, inspection, data analysis, auditing, and quality systems experience in a manufacturing environment.

What You'll Do

As the Quality Technician, you'll support quality assurance activities across the value stream while helping ensure products, processes, and documentation meet customer requirements and MCC quality standards.

As the Quality Technician, you'll support quality assurance activities across the value stream while helping ensure products, processes, and documentation meet customer requirements and MCC quality standards.
Comply with all company policies, safety standards, and quality procedures
Assist with equipment calibration, care, and documentation
Approve labels, processes, and materials prior to press runs
Approve roll-end retains saved by press operators
Assemble, update, and maintain color tolerance folders, color consistency files, and clear overlays
Collect, review, and analyze reject and quality data as assigned
Support the MCC Quality Management System, including document control and record maintenance
Perform internal audits as a member of MCC’s Internal Audit Team
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives and quality-related projects
Attend department meetings as scheduled
Work overtime as required and perform related duties as assigned

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone with quality or manufacturing experience who understands quality assurance principles and inspection techniques, works carefully within defined procedures, and can combine strong attention to detail with analytical, mathematical, communication, and organizational skills.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent with three or more years of quality or manufacturing experience; printing industry experience preferred
Working knowledge of quality assurance principles and inspection techniques
Ability to read rulers, interpret measurements, and successfully complete color hue testing
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, with strong analytical and mathematical skills
Strong attention to detail with the ability to remain focused and follow procedures throughout the shift
Ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks, and complete assignments through to completion
Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Familiarity with ISO 9001 standards; ASQ certification a plus but not required
Ability to meet the physical demands of the role, including frequent standing and walking, occasional climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling, and regularly lifting up to 50 pounds
Vision requirements include close, distance, color, peripheral, and depth perception, with the ability to adjust focus

Career Growth

This position provides an opportunity to deepen your experience in quality assurance, inspection techniques, reject and quality data analysis, document control, internal auditing, and continuous improvement while supporting MCC's Quality Management System in a manufacturing environment.

title: Facilities Maintenance Associate
description:
Indian Creek School is an independent, co-ed day school in which 600 students age 3 to Grade 12 partner with innovative teachers in an outstanding educational program. Located on a beautiful, 114-acre campus in Crownsville, Maryland (just north of Annapolis), ICS students are nurtured and known as individuals while being challenged to discover their passions, purpose, and potential. The School's vision statement reads: Indian Creek is the premier independent school in the Annapolis area where kindness is currency, well-being is priority, and excellence in education is relentlessly pursued. The Indian Creek community is actively committed to diversity, equity, and belonging, and we foster an inclusive environment in which students feel understood, valued, respected, and affirmed.

ICS seeks faculty and staff who support our mission and values, who are committed to nurturing learners as individuals, and who are looking to join a vibrant community of professionals who are passionate about education. Faculty and staff are offered meaningful opportunities for professional growth. Because we are a small school, every member of our community plays a critical role in making sure the institution lives up to its mission.

This position is full time, 12 months and reports to the Director of Facilities. The preferred schedule is 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.; however, the School is open to discussing a later eight-hour shift with a qualified candidate.

Requirements

The Facilities Maintenance Associate helps operate and care for Indian Creek School’s buildings, grounds, athletic and performing arts facilities, and campus infrastructure each day. The associate performs routine repairs and preventive maintenance, responds to maintenance requests using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (FMX), and prepares spaces for daily operations, school events, and facility rentals. The position also conducts safety and security checks, identifies concerns that require specialized attention, and helps keep the campus safe, clean, and ready for students, employees, families, and visitors. Success in this role requires initiative, sound judgment, and flexibility as campus needs change throughout the day.

This position works around students during the school day. The associate must maintain appropriate professional boundaries, follow school policies on student safety and conduct, and arrange work so that tools, chemicals, and active work areas are secured and instruction is disrupted as little as possible. The employee must complete required school training and follow applicable Maryland reporting obligations. Indian Creek School welcomes candidates who will contribute to an inclusive and respectful school community.

Primary Responsibilities

Buildings and work orders

  • Check spaces, doors, and entry points at the start of the day and throughout the shift; correct routine issues, make hazards safe when possible, and report safety or security concerns promptly.
  • Perform minor carpentry, patching and painting, furniture adjustments, and repairs to doors, hardware, fixtures, and basic plumbing; replace lamps, filters, and similar components.
  • Complete scheduled preventive maintenance and use FMX to receive and prioritize work orders, record completed work, update requestors, and document follow-up needs or parts required.
  • Assist with contractor access, site preparation, and follow-up for outside repairs as directed by the Director of Facilities.

Events and campus safety

  • Set up and break down tables, chairs, equipment, and spaces for assemblies, athletics, school events, and facility rentals; coordinate work around classes and the changing school calendar.
  • Help prepare for and respond to snow, ice, severe weather, and facility emergencies; support drills and campus operations.
  • Follow Indian Creek School standard operating procedures, recognized maintenance practices, and applicable OSHA and other safety requirements. Use tools and materials safely, secure work areas around students, and complete all required training as directed by the Director of Facilities.

Grounds and daily operations

  • Support the dedicated grounds crew as needed with entrances, walkways, parking areas, outdoor spaces, athletic fields, and seasonal grounds tasks, including snow and ice removal.
  • Supplement the cleaning teams when needed, including spill response, waste and recycling removal, cleaning and sanitizing spaces, and replenishing supplies.
  • Move and arrange classroom and office furniture, supplies, and equipment; help with receiving and placing deliveries when needed.

Qualifications

  • At least one year of experience in building or facilities maintenance or a related trade, or an equivalent combination of experience and training. Experience in a school or other occupied campus is a plus.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritize competing needs, complete work to a high standard, and recognize when to seek direction or a licensed specialist.
  • Comfortable using or quickly learning digital systems and applications, including Outlook, FMX, HVAC and lighting controls, and the school’s student information system. Able to use them to communicate, manage work orders, check calendars and other authorized information, and make building system adjustments within the scope of the role.
  • Working knowledge of common hand and power tools and basic repairs, with the ability to follow safety information and equipment instructions.
  • Strong interpersonal and organizational skills, with clear written and verbal communication. Ability to collaborate, build positive working relationships with students, colleagues, families, visitors, and vendors, and adapt to planned and immediate needs.
  • A valid driver’s license and ability to meet the school’s driving requirements. A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred.
  • Successful completion of required federal and state background checks and the MSDE Employment History Review.

Schedule and physical demands

This is a 12-month, full-time hourly position for an 8-hour shift, Monday through Friday. Flexibility is required, as occasional early morning, evening, weekend, overtime, or weather-related work may be needed for events, athletics, snow removal, campus emergencies, or other operational needs. The position involves extended standing and walking; bending, kneeling, reaching, and ladder use; working indoors and outdoors in varying Maryland weather; and safely operating maintenance and grounds equipment. The employee must be able to lift and carry up to 50 pounds and move heavier items with assistance or equipment.

Benefits

Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate's years of experience at an educational institution, relevant experience, and overall skillset. Candidates will be offered a competitive salary, eligible for overtime, and within the range of $52,000 - $58,000 dependent on experience. Salary will be prorated based off start date in the 2026-2027 school year.

In addition to the annual salary, Indian Creek School offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as life insurance, critical illness and accident coverage, and both short- and long-term disability for the employee and their eligible dependents. title: Mechanical Assembler
description:
The Mechanical Assembler is responsible for the installation and assembly of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and structural components on production equipment. Working as part of a collaborative assembly team, this position ensures equipment is assembled accurately, safely, and efficiently to meet production schedules and quality standards. The Mechanical Assembler reports directly to the Assembly Lead and Plant Supervisor.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Read, interpret, and follow blueprints, diagrams, engineering drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and written or verbal work instructions to accurately assemble equipment and products.

  • Safely operate hand tools, power tools, pneumatic tools, forklifts, and overhead cranes.
  • Adhere to all safety policies, procedures, and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) requirements during equipment assembly and operation.
  • Perform in-process and final quality inspections to verify products meet established quality standards and specifications.
  • Rework, modify, or repair equipment as required to incorporate engineering changes or correct identified issues.
  • Maintain tools, equipment, and workstations in good working condition.
  • Identify and recommend opportunities for continuous improvement in assembly processes, efficiency, and product quality.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment at all times.
  • Collaborate effectively with team members, engineering, supply chain and supervisors to achieve production goals and timelines.

Requirements

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, blueprints, and assembly documentation.
  • Ability to read and use a tape measure.
  • Experience using hand tools and power tools.
  • Ability to safely operate forklifts and overhead cranes, or willingness to obtain required certifications.
  • Ability to climb a ladder and work safety at required heights.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to follow safety procedures and work instructions consistently.
  • Capable of lifting, carrying, and maneuvering materials and components as required.

  • Perform welding, fabrication, and heavy rigging activities as required.
  • Safely operate shop equipment, including drill presses, small mills, band saws, forklifts, and overhead cranes.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical assembly issues and make necessary adjustments to ensure proper fit, alignment, and machine function.

  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment while complying with established quality, safety, and workplace procedures.
  • Work collaboratively with team members to support production schedules, quality standards, and project requirements.

Qualifications

  • Journeyman’s card or completion of an apprenticeship program preferred.
  • Experience building at least two machine models with the ability to independently complete most assemblies.
  • High level of mechanical skill with knowledge of machine assembly and precision inspection techniques.
  • Working knowledge of blueprints, schematics, and job instructions.
  • Knowledge of welding, fabrication, and heavy rigging.
  • Ability to accurately use and read precision measuring equipment.
  • Basic shop math skills.
  • Ability to safely operate hand tools, power tools, and applicable shop equipment.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with a team-oriented approach.
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and email.

  • Ability to work overtime and occasional weekends as needed.
  • Ability to maintain a safe and clean work environment while complying with all applicable quality, safety, and workplace policies and procedures.

title: Senior Commercial Executive
description:
About the Group

What’s Possible is the only harmonious group exclusively for marketers at entrepreneurial brands. It invests in, and supports, marketing services businesses in the UK, Europe and US.

At the heart of the group is The Specialist Works, one of the UK’s largest independent media agencies.

The group also includes What’s Possible Creative. Through its investment arm, Make Possible, the group invests in marketing services start-ups – including retail media specialist Vector and US retail media business Connections.

Role Overview

We are looking for an ambitious Senior Commercial Executive to join our Commercial team.

This is a highly visible role offering exposure to senior leadership, major client relationships, commercial negotiations, contract management, and new business pitches across the Group.

Working closely with the Group Commercial Director, you will take day-to-day ownership of a broad portfolio of commercial and contractual activity, helping to shape commercial outcomes, protect business interests and support sustainable growth across the Group.

Alongside assisting the Group Commercial Director in the management of all commercial and contractual work, you will play an important role in developing and supervising the Commercial Executive, helping to shape the future capability and growth of the Commercial team.

This role would suit someone with experience in commercial management, contract review and negotiation, procurement, business operations, or a similar commercially focused environment who is looking to accelerate their career while gaining exposure to all aspects of a modern media and marketing services business.

About the Team

The Commercial Department forms a key part of the Business Partner team within What's Possible Group. We oversee commercial and contractual arrangements involving clients, partners and third parties, supporting businesses across the Group including The Specialist Works, Connections, Ireland, and our Make Possible businesses.

Our role is to ensure commercial agreements are robust, commercially sustainable, operationally deliverable and aligned to the wider strategic objectives of the business.

Requirements

Commercial and Contractual Management

  • Work with the Group Commercial Director in the preparation, review, negotiation, and administration of a wide range of commercial documentation, including NDAs, DPAs, client agreements, variations, statements of work and partner contracts.
  • Review contractual terms, identify risks and opportunities, and provide practical commercial recommendations.
  • Manage contract execution processes through DocuSign and maintain accurate commercial records and documentation.
  • Produce clear commercial summaries and contract briefings for internal stakeholders.
  • Monitor contract renewals, notice periods, key obligations, and commercial commitments.
  • Ensure all elements of client commercial arrangements are effectively communicated and understood across the business.

Commercial Support and Negotiation

  • Take ownership of smaller client commercial projects and negotiations independently.
  • Support larger and more complex commercial negotiations alongside the Group Commercial Director.
  • Assist in developing innovative, commercially sustainable pricing and remuneration models.
  • Support client, procurement, and legal discussions throughout negotiation processes.
  • Work closely with Finance regarding payment terms, credit considerations, and commercial reconciliations.
  • Identify, manage, and appropriately escalate legal and commercial risks.

New Business and Growth

  • Support new business pitches, including proposal development, contractual reviews and commercial modelling including helping to build bespoke commercial solutions tailored to client requirements.
  • Work with internal teams to cost projects and evaluate commercial viability.
  • Contribute to innovative commercial structures that support growth while protecting business profitability.

Commercial Governance and Reporting

  • Help maintain key commercial databases, trackers, and governance processes.
  • Support commercial reporting, profitability analysis, and business insight initiatives.
  • Identify emerging commercial risks and escalate appropriately.
  • Monitor key contractual milestones, renewal dates, and compliance requirements.
  • Help drive continual improvements in commercial processes, controls, and documentation

Team Leadership and Development

  • Help provide day-to-day supervision, support, and quality control for the Commercial Level 1 Executive.
  • Help allocate and prioritise workload across the Commercial team to ensure efficient delivery against business requirements.
  • Assist in coaching, training, and developing the Commercial Executive, helping build commercial, contractual, and operational knowledge.
  • Review work produced by the Commercial Executive, providing constructive feedback and ensuring high standards of accuracy and quality.
  • Support performance management, objective setting, and ongoing development planning.
  • Help build a collaborative, high-performing and continually developing Commercial function.

What We’re Looking For

Essential:

  • Practical experience reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements.
  • Strong commercial awareness and sound business judgement.
  • Experience working within a fast-paced commercial environment.
  • Excellent writing, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • High attention to detail and excellent document management skills.
  • Strong Excel, Word, and PowerPoint skills.
  • Confidence working with senior stakeholders both internally and externally.

Desirable:

  • Experience within media, marketing services, advertising, procurement, or professional services.
  • Knowledge of GDPR and data protection principles.
  • Experience of commercial modelling, pricing, or profitability analysis.
  • Familiarity with DocuSign or similar contract management tools.
  • Exposure to procurement or legal negotiation processes.

We are looking for someone who is:

  • Commercially minded and naturally curious.
  • Proactive and solutions focused.
  • Highly organised with exceptional attention to detail, able to identify inconsistencies, risks and opportunities within complex contracts, commercial arrangements, and business documentation.
  • Comfortable reviewing, interpreting, and working with contracts, legal documentation, and formal commercial agreements, with the ability to translate complex language into clear, practical business recommendations.
  • Eager to learn and develop.
  • Able to balance commercial opportunity with sensible risk management.

Benefits

We provide an exciting, fast paced, people first environment that allows everyone to grow, learn and thrive.

We work a 9-day fortnight, meaning staff have every other Friday off!

We’ve built a benefits package that invests in our employees’ long-term personal and professional growth and wellbeing.

Our Values

o Passion: You share your excitement about what drives you

o Inquisitiveness: Ask “what’s possible?”. Ask “why not?”

o Caring: Be a good professional, a good colleague and a good human

o Knowledge: Know plenty. Share it. Learn more.

And we live them every day #IamPICK

Social and Environmental Commitment

At What’s Possible Group, our mission is to build a group our people are proud of. Proud of what we deliver to clients. Proud of how we treat each other. Proud of our commitment to people, planet and profit.

Having rolled out a What’s Possible University with learning modules & policies, including anti bribery & corruption, DE&I and code of ethics, our people have continuous personal development, and the group is continuously improving.

We are dedicated to embedding social and environmental responsibility into every aspect of our business. You'll contribute to initiatives that promote social equity, diversity, and inclusion within our workplace and in the content, we create, whilst actively supporting and promoting sustainable best practice by, continuously working to minimise waste, (for example, water & cardboard recycling), prioritise eco-friendly suppliers, (for example, renewable energy switch), and promote remote work to reduce carbon emissions.

Your role will include supporting these efforts by helping to implement green office practices, coordinating initiatives that enhance our corporate social responsibility, and ensuring our operations align with our values of sustainability and social responsibility.

Sound good to you? Then get in touch.

At The What’s Possible Group our culture, our creativity and our passion is powered by people. People just like you. Diversity and difference drive innovation, not only for us but also for our clients and is at the heart of everything that we do.

title: Desktop Support Technician
description:
Position Summary

The Desktop Support Technician provides hands-on, customer-focused technical support for R+L Carriers users and workplace technology. This role diagnoses and resolves incidents involving Windows endpoints, business applications, peripherals, printing, and connectivity; prepares and deploys standard hardware; and ensures each user receives timely, professional service.

The technician owns assigned support work from intake through documented resolution, using the IT service-management process and established Desktop Support procedures. The role works both onsite and remotely, supports users across corporate and field locations, and collaborates with infrastructure, security, applications, service desk, vendors, and business partners when issues require escalation or coordinated action.

The Desktop Support Technician is expected to operate with sound judgment, protect company information, follow endpoint and asset-management standards, and contribute to a dependable, consistent end-user computing experience. The role combines strong troubleshooting ability with clear communication, disciplined documentation, and a willingness to improve processes that affect users and the support team.

Key Responsibilities

Responsibility AreaAccountabilities
End-User Support and Incident Resolution

  • Provide timely onsite and remote technical support for Windows computers, business applications, Microsoft 365 services, printers, scanners, conferencing equipment, and related peripherals.

  • Diagnose incidents using sound troubleshooting practices; resolve issues at the appropriate support level and escalate promptly when infrastructure, security, application, or vendor involvement is required.

  • Communicate clearly with users regarding issue status, expected next steps, workarounds, and resolution; maintain a professional, customer-first service experience.

  • Document troubleshooting actions, resolutions, and meaningful user communication in the IT service-management system; identify recurring issues and bring them forward for review.

Endpoint Deployment and Lifecycle

  • Prepare, image, configure, test, deploy, replace, and recover desktop and laptop hardware in accordance with approved build standards and security requirements.

  • Support new-hire onboarding, employee moves, hardware refreshes, and separations by ensuring equipment, access requests, accessories, and documentation are completed accurately and on time.

  • Perform hardware break/fix, warranty coordination, component replacement, and vendor repair follow-up; verify devices are returned to service in a reliable and supportable condition.

  • Assist with endpoint-management and deployment activities, including approved software installation, configuration changes, patching support, and post-deployment validation.

Multi-Site and Field Support

  • Provide effective support for users at corporate, Tech Center, terminals, and other R+L locations through a combination of onsite visits, remote tools, and coordinated shipment or vendor service.

  • Prioritize work based on business impact, service commitments, and operational need; communicate conflicts and risks to the Desktop Support Manager promptly.

  • Support workplace technology and local peripherals in operational environments while maintaining appropriate safety, security, and professional standards.

Asset and Inventory Stewardship

  • Record and maintain accurate asset information, including serial number, internal asset identifier, hostname, assignment, location, and lifecycle status in the approved asset-management system.

  • Coordinate with inventory personnel to maintain proper control of stock, returns, accessories, and shipping materials; follow established chain-of-custody and return procedures.

  • Assist with physical inventory counts, hardware audits, refresh planning, and the disposition of retired equipment in accordance with company standards.

Security, Compliance, and Standardization

  • Verify endpoint compliance with approved operating-system, security-agent, encryption, VPN, certificate, and management-agent requirements before devices are placed into service.

  • Follow least-privilege, data-protection, and change-control practices; immediately report suspected security events, lost devices, or material compliance concerns through established channels.

  • Apply approved standards consistently and identify opportunities to reduce support risk, improve endpoint reliability, and strengthen the user experience.

Team Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

  • Work collaboratively with Desktop Support teammates, Service Desk, Infrastructure, Security, application teams, and vendors to resolve issues and improve service delivery.

  • Create and maintain useful knowledge articles, support procedures, configuration notes, and deployment documentation that enable consistent team execution.

  • Participate in team meetings, training, project work, and continuous-improvement efforts; share technical knowledge and support peers as business needs require.


Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent required

  • Associate degree, technical diploma, or relevant coursework in Information Technology, Computer Support, or a related field preferred

  • CompTIA A+, Microsoft, or comparable endpoint-support certification preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered

Experience

  • 2 or more years of hands-on desktop, deskside, field, or technical-support experience in a business environment; enterprise or multi-site experience preferred

  • Demonstrated experience troubleshooting Windows computers, common productivity applications, printers, peripherals, and basic network-connectivity issues

  • Experience deploying and supporting laptops and desktops, including imaging, software installation, hardware replacement, and user setup

  • Experience using an IT service-management/ticketing system and maintaining accurate work notes and asset records

  • Experience supporting logistics, transportation, manufacturing, warehouse, or another operations-intensive environment preferred

Technical Competencies

  • Windows 11 support, configuration, and troubleshooting

  • Microsoft 365 desktop applications and collaboration tools; familiarity with Exchange/Outlook, OneDrive, and Teams or Webex support

  • PC and laptop hardware, docking stations, monitors, printers, scanners, and common peripherals

  • Basic Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID concepts, including user, group, device, and password-related support activities

  • Endpoint imaging, software deployment, remote-support tools, and endpoint-management platforms such as Ivanti or equivalent

  • Basic TCP/IP, Wi-Fi, VPN, DNS, and network-troubleshooting concepts sufficient to isolate and route end-user issues appropriately

  • Asset-management and inventory-control practices, including accurate serial-number and assignment documentation

  • Security fundamentals: endpoint protection, encryption, MFA, certificate/VPN requirements, and safe handling of company data

Professional Competencies

  • Customer service: listens carefully, communicates plainly, and follows through on commitments to users and teammates

  • Problem solving: applies structured troubleshooting, uses available knowledge and tools effectively, and recognizes when escalation is appropriate

  • Organization and accountability: manages multiple priorities, maintains complete documentation, and takes ownership of assigned work

  • Collaboration: works constructively with technical and non-technical partners; shares knowledge and supports team standards

  • Adaptability: remains effective during changing priorities, operational disruptions, and technology rollouts

  • Physical capability: able to move and install computer equipment, work at user locations, and travel to company sites as business needs require

title: Project Lead
description:
Winthrop Technologies is Europe’s only dedicated data centre delivery partner, offering full turnkey solutions from design through to construction and commissioning. Headquartered in Dublin, we deliver projects across Europe and have become the most trusted name in our sector.

We are currently seeking an experienced Project Lead to join our project team in Blanchardstown, Dublin 15. The Project Lead will be responsible for the overall management and successful delivery of the project, ensuring it is completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. The role requires strong leadership, commercial awareness, and technical expertise, with an emphasis on effective communication and stakeholder coordination.

  • Coordinate and oversee scheduling consultant reviews and ensure integration with project controls.
  • Review and approve invoices, payment applications, and retention payments.
  • Manage the handover process to the client, including close-out documentation, warranties, and final deliverables.

Requirements

  • Minimum 10 years’ experience in a similar role.
  • Strong organisational, communication, and time management skills.
  • Proficient in MS Word, Excel, and other relevant project management tools.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, manage subcontractors, and coordinate multidisciplinary project activities.
  • Commercially astute, with a strong understanding of project financial management and cost control.
  • Capable of working under pressure to meet demanding schedules while maintaining the highest quality and safety standards.

Benefits

  • Opportunity to work for a market leader in the Data centre industry
  • Working on large scale data centre projects
  • Collaborative team working environments
  • Career progression and development supported
  • Competitive salary packages

title: Service Supervisor
description:
Why choose us?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.


Position Summary

The Service Supervisor supports the daily operation of the front end by providing leadership and direction to associates while ensuring customers receive friendly, efficient, and professional service. This position helps maintain smooth checkout operations, coordinates front-end coverage, assists with customer concerns, and ensures company procedures and service standards are consistently followed.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide leadership and direction to cashiers, courtesy clerks, self-checkout attendants, and other front-end associates.

  • Monitor self-checkout operations and ensure customers receive prompt assistance.
  • Assist customers with questions, price discrepancies, refunds, and other service-related concerns.
  • Resolve customer concerns professionally and involve management when additional assistance is required.
  • Assist with cash-handling procedures, register tills, pickups, and other front-end financial responsibilities as assigned.
  • Help ensure associates follow proper cash-handling and register procedures.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and properly supplied checkout lanes, customer service areas, self-checkout stations, and store entrances.
  • Coordinate courtesy clerk responsibilities, including bagging, cart retrieval, carry-outs, cleaning, and other assigned duties.
  • Monitor shopping cart availability and ensure carts are retrieved as needed.
  • Provide training, coaching, and ongoing support to front-end associates.
  • Ensure associates follow customer service expectations, company policies, and workplace safety procedures.
  • Communicate equipment issues, staffing concerns, service opportunities, and other operational needs to store leadership.
  • Assist with opening and closing front-end responsibilities as assigned.
  • Support store leadership with additional operational responsibilities when needed.
  • Support other areas of the store as necessary and contribute to a positive, team-oriented work environment.
Leadership Expectations
  • Lead by example and maintain a professional, positive, and customer-focused attitude.
  • Provide associates with clear direction and follow up to ensure assigned responsibilities are completed.
  • Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the front end.
  • Coach associates on customer service, productivity, accuracy, and department expectations.
  • Recognize strong performance and help identify opportunities for associate development.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, urgency, and consistent customer service.
  • Respond quickly to changes in customer traffic and adjust front-end coverage accordingly.
  • Maintain composure and professionalism when handling difficult customer situations.
  • Communicate effectively with associates, department leadership, and store management.
  • Help create a welcoming environment for both customers and associates.
Qualifications
  • Previous retail, grocery, customer service, or related experience preferred.
  • Previous front-end, cashier, or leadership experience preferred.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to provide direction and support to multiple associates.
  • Basic understanding of cash-handling and register procedures preferred.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to resolve customer concerns calmly and professionally.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.
  • Must be dependable, professional, organized, and able to demonstrate good judgment.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule based on business needs, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Ability to bend, reach, squat, push, pull, and perform repetitive motions.
  • Ability to lift and move products, supplies, and front-end equipment as required.
  • Ability to push and retrieve shopping carts as needed.
  • Ability to move throughout the store frequently to assist customers and associates.
  • Ability to perform register, customer service, and other front-end duties based on business needs.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Position Summary
The Office Administrator plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day operations of the branch. This position serves as the administrative hub of the office, providing support across accounting, customer service, office coordination, and operational administration.
The successful candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and customer-focused, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and professionalism. Working closely with branch leadership, sales, operations, and customers, the Office Administrator helps ensure efficient branch operations and an exceptional customer experience.
Key Responsibilities
Accounting & Financial Administration

Process accounts payable transactions, including coding, allocation, and recording of vendor invoices.
Process accounts receivable transactions, customer payments, and credit card sales.
Prepare and issue customer invoices and assist with collections activities as required.
Reconcile invoices, purchase orders, shipping documents, and supporting records to ensure accuracy.
Track project-related costs, including freight, brokerage, product costs, and credits.
Assist with month-end reporting, reconciliations, accruals, and other accounting activities.
Support inventory-related transactions and branch transfer reconciliations.

Office Administration

Serve as the first point of contact for visitors, customers, vendors, and employees.
Answer and direct incoming calls and inquiries in a professional and timely manner.
Prepare, process, and maintain customer and vendor documentation, including invoices, acknowledgements, packing slips, and tracking information.
Coordinate customer setup and credit approval documentation.
Organize and maintain electronic and physical filing systems.
Manage office supplies, kitchen inventory, and general office requirements.
Assist with preparing reports, presentations, and business documentation as required.

Customer & Team Support

Deliver exceptional customer service to internal and external stakeholders.
Liaise with customers, vendors, sales teams, warehouse personnel, and other departments to resolve issues and ensure timely follow-up.
Assist with branch communications, meetings, events, and employee activities as required.
Support branch leadership and team members with general administrative activities.
Maintain a professional, welcoming, and organized office environment.

Operations Support

Assist with inventory administration and inventory count processes.
Support shipping, receiving, and logistics documentation requirements.
Monitor operational documentation and ensure records are accurate and complete.
Identify opportunities to improve administrative processes and operational efficiency.

Qualifications
Education & Experience

High school diploma or equivalent required.
Post-secondary education in Office Administration, Business Administration, Accounting, Bookkeeping, or a related field is considered an asset.
Minimum 3 years of experience in an administrative, office coordination, or office management role.
Experience with accounts payable, accounts receivable, invoicing, or bookkeeping is preferred.

Skills & Competencies

Exceptional organizational and time-management skills.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong customer service and relationship-building abilities.
Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and Teams.
Experience with accounting or ERP software is considered an asset.
Ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment.

What Success Looks Like

Creating a seamless office experience – ensuring the branch operates efficiently through well-organized administrative processes, accurate documentation, and proactive coordination of daily office activities.
Delivering accurate and timely financial administration – processing invoices, payments, reconciliations, and month-end activities with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.
Providing exceptional customer and stakeholder support – becoming a trusted first point of contact for customers, vendors, and employees through responsiveness, professionalism, and effective problem resolution.
Building strong internal partnerships – developing collaborative relationships with sales, operations, warehouse, and regional teams to support business objectives and ensure smooth branch operations.
Maintaining a high standard of organization and accountability – keeping records, files, reporting, and office systems current, accurate, and audit-ready while consistently meeting deadlines and commitments.
Driving operational efficiency and continuous improvement – identifying opportunities to streamline processes, improve workflows, and enhance the overall effectiveness of branch administration.
Contributing to a positive workplace culture – demonstrating professionalism, ownership, teamwork, and a service-oriented approach that supports employee engagement and overall branch success.

title: Director, Strategic Program Management
description:
The Opportunity: ​ At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As the Director, Strategic Program Management, you will play a key role in shaping and delivering a portfolio of strategic initiatives within Individual Insurance. From the earliest stages of program development, you will help define strategic direction, oversee the successful execution of interconnected projects, and ensure initiatives achieve intended business outcomes. In addition to leading a team of project professionals, you will be responsible for program budgeting and expense management, partnering with leaders across the organization to develop annual financial plans, monitor results, and drive accountability. This is an exciting opportunity to influence enterprise-wide initiatives, collaborate with senior leaders and external partners, and help transform strategic priorities into measurable results.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements: This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.
What you’ll do:

Lead a team of Project Managers and Business Analysts to deliver business outcomes in support of strategic objectives and ensure excellence in program and project execution.
Manage a portfolio of integrated projects within a strategic program, ensuring successful delivery to desired quality, on time and within budget.
Partner with business and technical leaders, and all project stakeholders to plan delivery to strategic direction, manage priorities and implementation plans for all program initiatives.
Coordinate cross-functional teams across business units, corporate functions, external vendors, and third-party contractors to drive project success.
Develop and maintain real-time reporting, program and project plans, schedules, and progress updates for strategic initiatives to Executive teams, project leaders and all project stakeholders.
Lead vendor assessment processes, including RFP evaluations, recommendations, and the development of statements of work.
Track program risks, issues, and dependencies, driving timely resolution and maintaining momentum across multiple initiatives.
Oversee program budgeting, forecasting, and expense management, including developing annual plans and monitoring financial performance throughout the year.

What you’ll bring:

Deep experience leading large-scale programs or portfolios of interconnected initiatives across an organization.
Proven ability to manage complex projects while balancing multiple high-priority initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Experience working with technology-based platforms and a passion for driving innovation and new initiatives.
Extensive experience in leading, coaching and developing teams of Project Managers and Business Analysts
Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, including executive leadership, external vendors, and business partners.
Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to translate long-term objectives into actionable plans and measurable outcomes.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the capacity to evaluate legal documents, RFP responses, and complex business challenges.
Strong financial acumen, including expertise in budgeting, forecasting, expense management, and cost-benefit analysis.
High emotional intelligence, a strong sense of urgency, and the ability to move projects forward through collaboration, patience, and assertive leadership.

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

We’re committed to fair pay and an inclusive, accessible hiring experience. If you need accommodations or alternative formats at any stage, just reach out to us at careers@equitable.ca. We’re happy to help.

title: Store Director
description:
Position Purpose:

Monitors, enforces, and supports execution of the division merchandising plan for their department in assigned stores.

  1. Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Overall management responsibility for operation of retail grocery store, including store performance, control of cash, inventory and security, customer services, and management of staff.

  • Track, analyze and take action to improve store performance by forecasting of weekly/daily sales goals and meeting or exceeding established goals. Communicate sales goals, department performance and sales opportunities with staff to ensure positive results.

  • Forecast, schedule, and monitor labor to be consistent with store sales and productivity guidelines and wage budgets; create action plan to address cost control issues.

  • Develop and direct execution of strategies to improve product placement and appearance.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance, sick pay (accrued based on hours worked), PTO/Vacation Pay (accrued based on hours worked), paid holidays, bereavement pay, and retirement benefits (pension and/or 401k eligibility). title: Ophthalmic Technician - Retina
description:
Ophthalmology Experience Required

A career that changes lives.

SightMD is a rapidly growing integrated ophthalmic provider group, extending the reach of exceptional eye care to patients across New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, and Massachusetts. With over 127 eye care providers and the convenience of 60 locations, our commitment to delivering unparalleled services is at the heart of everything we do. As we embark on our mission, we are actively seeking teammates who are eager to contribute to our legacy of eye excellence, a tradition that spans more than 50 years.

Position Summary:

As a Ophthalmic Technician (Retina), you will play a vital role as an assistant to our physicians. You will be cross trained to perform a range of administrative and clinical duties. These duties include preparing the patient to see the physician, preparing examination rooms, performing basic and routine vision screening examinations, administering eye medications, cleaning, and maintaining ophthalmic instruments and assisting physicians during minor surgical and laser procedures.

Job Duties & Essential Functions:

Patient Interaction & Clinical Intake

  • Greet and communicate with patients and their families in a manner consistent with caring and respect.
  • Initiate patient evaluations by accurately documenting the chief complaint, history of present illness, review of systems, and all pertinent information.
  • Coordinate and obtain prior authorizations for medications in accordance with insurance requirements to ensure timely patient access to prescribed treatments.

Pre-Exam & Diagnostic Testing

  • Perform pre-exam testing, including visual acuity assessment (with pinhole and glare testing), confrontational visual fields, extraocular muscle testing, pupillary evaluation, tonometry, angle assessment, and dilation.
  • Conduct advanced diagnostic testing such as OCT, fundus photography, IOL Master, Pentacam, A-scan, B-scan, Wave Scan/Vario, keratometry, lensometry, and visual field testing.
  • Perform specialized testing as requested, including color vision screening, stereopsis, dry eye testing, optical biometry, and refractometry.

Procedure & Treatment Support

  • Assist with in-office minor surgical procedures and laser treatments.
  • Complete prescription refill requests as authorized by the physician, ensuring proper documentation in the patient chart.
  • Track, document, and communicate laboratory results to physicians and patients promptly, ensuring accuracy and continuity of care.
  • Educate patients on the use of medications and provide pre- and post-operative instructions as directed by the physician.
  • Assist with contact lens fittings and provide patient instruction on insertion, removal, and lens care.

Equipment & Inventory Management

  • Maintain and manage inventory of ophthalmic supplies, pharmaceuticals, and instruments.
  • Inspect and assist with the maintenance of clinical examination equipment, report damage, coordinate repairs, and request replacements as necessary.
  • Assist with cleaning surgical instruments in preparation for sterilization.
  • Properly shut down and clean diagnostic testing equipment as needed.
  • Check and record medical refrigerator temperatures daily; monitor supply dates and manage inventory accordingly.

Clinic Readiness & Administrative Support

  • Open and close exam rooms daily, including cleaning equipment, charging devices, and securing instruments.
  • Assist with opening and closing the clinic as needed.
  • Follow all safety protocols and clinic procedures.
  • Monitor and respond to work emails; utilize shared tools such as Google Drive to stay informed throughout the workday.
  • Maintain strict adherence to HIPAA regulations by safeguarding patient privacy and ensuring the confidentiality of all health information.

Professional Development

  • Participate in training and educational opportunities, including webinars and in-service sessions, to remain current with best practices.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned or directed by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum of one (1) year of experience as an Ophthalmic Technician
  • Certified Ophthalmic Assistant (COA) certification required or enrolled within one year and completion within two years of hire
  • Strong customer service skills with a professional and friendly demeanor.
  • Excellent organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities.
  • Skilled in problem-solving with strong attention to detail.
  • Comfortable engaging in face-to-face interactions with patients and staff.
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time

Work Schedule:

  • Rotating Schedule – including days, evenings and weekends

Hourly Pay Rate:

  • $24.50

Benefits:

We aim to take care of our teammates the same way we take care of our patients. All SightMD employees receive the following benefits:

  • Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance
  • Prescription Drug Coverage
  • Company Paid Term Life Insurance & Long-Term Disability
  • Supplemental Insurance Benefits
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Retirement Plan - 401(k)
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Paid Holidays
  • Career Development Programs

* All benefits are subject to eligibility requirements.

title: Clinical Intern - Main Cardiovascular Stepdown - Full Time - Nights
description:
The practice of nursing requires specialized knowledge, judgment, and skills to provide care to groups and individuals. The RN utilizes knowledge derived from the principles of biological, physical, behavioral, social, and nursing sciences to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate patient care. All care is provided based on the concepts inherent in the model of care for TCH which promotes an on-going partnership between patients and families and the team of healthcare providers. The care is culturally based and age specific. The RN adheres to American Nursing Association (ANA) code of ethics and to the scope of practice described in the Ohio Nurse Practice Act.

The Nursing Process

Assessment - Demonstrates the nursing skills to complete a holistic assessment of the patient’s physical, psychosocial, spiritual, and education needs utilizing The Christ Hospital Professional Practice Model.

1. Understands signs and symptoms and data related to the patient’s presenting needs and actual or potential nursing diagnosis.

2. Recognizes and appropriately reports to the physician and charge RN pertinent abnormal data and changes in the patient’s condition.

3. Utilizes appropriate handoff methods to collaborate with other healthcare team members to communicate pertinent data regarding patient’s physiological and psychological data.

4. Assesses patient, family, and environment for safety risks, proactively seeks out and performs safety initiatives.

Diagnosis and Planning - Utilizes collected data to establish and prioritize a list of actual, and potential, individualized patient problems and needs.

1. Prepares, coordinates, and revises multidisciplinary plan of care in collaboration with the patient and family to be supportive of the TCH model of care/Patient and Family Centered care. For each problem a measurable goal is set.

2. Communicates the plan of care utilizing SBAR and handoff processes with all team members.

3. Establish priorities of care, discusses plan of care during shift report, and participates in care conferences.

4. Initiates discharge planning upon admission, makes appropriate referrals consistent with the anticipated length of stay.

Implementation – The method of providing evidence based, quality care is based on assessed needs and standards of care while adhering to hospital policy and procedures to achieve set goals.

1. Performs and delegates nursing actions based on appropriate orders demonstrates critical thinking and accountability for appropriate implementation.

2. Provides ongoing, individualized holistic patient and family education based on needs and plan of care in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team.

3. Demonstrates critical thinking upon review of physician orders, making appropriate referrals, & contacts other health team professionals.

4. Responds to emergency situations that require an immediate, controlled precision in a skillful manner.

5. Implements measures to prevent contamination and/or transmission of disease to include the use of appropriate protective devices and equipment to prevent injury and maintain a safe environment.

Evaluation – Continuously evaluates nursing practice related to the plan of care in relation to the standards of care established through evidence-based literature and standards established by professional organization that have been built into order sets in the electronic medical record, the individual plan of care, and patient outcomes and goals.

1. Evaluates effectiveness of nursing care interventions, adjusts or continues with plan of care based on patient and family response.

2. Maintains continuity of care by continuous evaluation during ”handoff” report, rounding, and upon transfers to other specialty units and post care facilities.

Documentation

Nursing process is accurately and concisely documented in the patient’s electronic medical record reflecting the plan of care as implemented by the patient, family, and multidisciplinary team.

Documents information in a timely manner, according to hospital policy, to include the plan of care, accurate updates, teaching and the patients’ and family response to care.

Leadership and Professional Development

Demonstrates leadership skills such as the ability to motivate, educate, delegate, and mentor peers and other members of the healthcare team while effectively managing the care of patients and family members.

Assumes responsibility and accountability for professional growth and development. Contributes to the professional development of peers, colleagues, and others.

1. Participates in 75% of staff meetings and 75% of council meetings as appropriate.

2. Participates in unit based activities/initiatives for performance improvement, evidence based projects, and research as needed.

3. Participates in council activities and task forces to improve competencies of self, co-workers, and staff members related to patient care.

4. Supports self and peers in professional growth and development utilizing resources and opportunities within and outside of The Christ Hospital.

5. Participates in self and peer review activities to include the positive recognition of peers and staff on a regular basis.

6. Acts as a resource, educator and preceptor for multidisciplinary team members, staff and nursing students, continuously evaluating and documenting competency. .

7. Maintains competency in POC (point of care) testing for unit specific nursing practice.

8. The following are strongly encouraged:

a. Participation in the professional advancement program.

b. Certification specific to work area of professional practice when eligible.

c. Participation in chosen professional organizations and conferences.

d. Participation in development and maintenance of research activities.

e. Participation in community service activities.

Employee Responsibilities

Complies with organization and department policies and required training.

Completes all educational requirements to maintain competency related to specific population of patient and/or regulatory agencies (Healthstream education 100% on-time completion and attendance for annual education day).

Submits required tests and paperwork in a timely manner without management interventions.

Attendance

Follows the time and attendance policy; reports to work on time, maintains a good attendance record, has badge and uses it to clock in and out, makes requests for tie off as far in advance as possible, etc.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL:

Please describe any specialized knowledge or skills, which are REQUIRED to perform the position duties. Do not list personal credentials of the current jobholder that would not be required if the job were being filled. List any special education required for this position.

EDUCATION:

• TCH does hire AD and Diploma nurses; however all nurses hired after January 2010 must receive their BSN within 5 years of the date of hire. RN’s who were employed at TCH prior to January 2010, and have more than 20 years of experience as an RN are permitted to pursue their BSN on a voluntary basis.

  • A MSN or DNP are not required but supersede the requirement for the BSN.

YEARS OF EXPERIENCE: None required

REQUIRED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE: The RN demonstrates the knowledge, abilities, and skills to provide age and culturally specific patient care and education. The RN effectively communicates with peers, utilizes appropriate channels of communication and maintains absolute confidentiality. The RN maintains competence and demonstrates evidence of continuing professional growth. The RN demonstrates the ability to accept and implement change and the ability to work in a culturally diverse setting.

LICENSES & CERTIFICATIONS:

The RN holds a current licensure to practice nursing in Ohio. Membership in professional organizations is desirable. BLS certification is required prior to patient contact. ACLS is required within 6 months of hire in step-down and ICU areas. Certification in area of clinical specialty is expected within five years of eligibility.

title: CAPEX Project Manager
description:

This position manages industrial capital projects from concept and front-end planning through procurement, execution, commissioning, and closeout.

The successful candidate will bring strong project-management discipline, technical and commercial judgment, and the ability to independently drive complex, cross-functional projects involving equipment suppliers, contractors, facility modifications, and manufacturing operations.

Key Responsibilities:

title: Hardware/Packout/Trainee
description:

  • Ethics: Treats people with respect; works with integrity and ethically; upholds organizational values.​

  • Learning and Development: Actively engages in learning and development opportunities provided by the company to acquire new skills and improve proficiency in production processes.
  • Organizational Skills: Has strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize jobs when necessary, and maintain accurate records in a fast-paced environment.

description:

This role can be based out of one our main offices including: Stellarton, NS; Mississauga, ON. Calgary, AB, Burnaby, BC

We’re seeking a Subject Matter Expert (SME) who will lead both detection engineering and proactive threat hunting to design, implement, and continuously improve our detection logic and hunt operations across retail and enterprise environments. The role blends advanced SIEM/EDR content engineering with hypothesis‑driven hunts and actionable threat intelligence to build a threat‑informed defense.

Key Responsibilities
Detection Engineering

Design, author, and maintain high‑fidelity detection rules and behavioral analytics across SIEM/EDR (e.g., Azure Sentinel or Elastic Stack or Splunk SPL for detections and dashboards).
Parse/normalize diverse log sources (POS systems, payment gateways, e‑commerce platforms, cloud services, and network devices) to ensure consistent, log data.
Perform detection gap analysis, recommend architecture improvements, and document use cases in a detection content catalog/knowledge base.

Threat Hunting & Threat Intelligence

Lead hypothesis‑driven hunts using MITRE ATT&CK and behavioral analytics to uncover ransomware, data exfiltration, POS malware, supply‑chain compromises, card skimming, cloud misconfigurations, and insider fraud.
Integrate curated threat intelligence (including retail‑focused actors such as FIN6 and current ransomware groups) into hunting and detection pipelines; produce actionable reports and executive briefings.

Automation, SIEM/EDR Operations & Response

Build automation to streamline alert triage and response; optimize SIEM dashboards and data models for retail‑specific visibility.
Partner with IR/SOC to operationalize detections and hunts; track efficacy and continuously tune for false‑positive reduction.

Collaboration & Leadership

Collaborate closely with SOC, IR, and engineering teams; mentor junior analysts and lead knowledge‑sharing sessions.
Communicate status, risks, and outcomes to stakeholders; drive threat‑informed risk assessments and posture improvements.

Project & Program Management

Own end‑to‑end delivery of detection and hunting initiatives (scope, timelines, resources, deliverables) aligned to compliance and business objectives.

Qualifications & Requirements

SIEM/EDR Expertise: Advanced Splunk SPL; hands‑on with SIEM (Splunk, QRadar) and EDR tools.
Log Engineering: Proven experience normalizing/ingesting logs from POS, payment systems, e‑commerce, cloud, and network devices.
Threat‑Informed Defense: Ability to operationalize threat intelligence and conduct ATT&CK‑aligned hunts.
Cloud Security: Working knowledge of AWS, Azure, GCP in retail environments.
Compliance & Privacy: Strong understanding of PCI DSS for payment security monitoring and familiarity with GDPR/CCPA.
Scripting & Automation: Proficiency in Python and PowerShell for data parsing, enrichment, and workflow automation.
Retail Threats & Fraud: Experience with ransomware, card‑skimming, insider fraud, loyalty‑program and e‑commerce fraud patterns.

Preferred Certifications
GIAC GCDA, GCIA, GCFA, GCTI; OSCP; PMP (or equivalent).
#LI-Hybrid #LI-VJ1

Increased ATT&CK coverage and validated detections for priority TTPs.
Reduced mean‑time‑to‑detect (MTTD) and false‑positive rates through tuning and automation.

Regular delivery of high‑quality hunt reports, executive briefings, and detection content with measurable impact.

title: Electrothermal Modeling Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
GM Performance Power Units - Concord, NC
Electrothermal Modeling Engineer Intern - Onsite
Date of Internship: Summer 2027

Job Summary: GM Performance Power Units is seeking a motivated Electrothermal Modeling Engineer Intern to join our Energy Store team in Concord, NC. This internship will deliver a coupled thermal-ECM cell model in Star-CCM+, validated to cycler data, so pack thermal design can iterate on cell candidates inside the existing CFD workflow. You'll work alongside the cell test technician and Energy Store engineers, with primary focus on building and validating the coupled thermal-ECM model in Star-CCM+.

Key Responsibilities

Integrate battery cell electrical and thermal Reduced Order Models (ROMs) into the Star-CCM+ Battery module, coupled to the pack thermal solver, such that cell candidates can be iterated inside the existing CFD workflow
Set up and tune the coupled thermal-electrical simulation: mesh independence, boundary conditions, solver convergence, and residual monitoring for the conjugate heat-transfer problem.
Extract Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) parameters (R0, R1, C1, optional 2nd-order branch, OCV) from battery cycler data, with quantified uncertainty across SoC x temperature.
Correlate simulated cell voltage and surface temperature from the coupled model against measured drive-profile data to defined error targets.
Perform a sensitivity study on the top three model parameters and document their impact on coupled thermal predictions.
Author a repeatable model-calibration SOP validated by an independent engineer.
Present modeling progress and validation results at a mid-program readout and a final review to senior Energy Store and Thermal engineers.
Archive all raw data, processed data, models, and documentation per program naming convention.
Additional tasks as needed.

Required Qualifications

Enrolled in an BSc, MSc, MEng, or PhD program in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, or a closely related discipline, with an anticipated graduation date from Dec 2027 – May 2028.
Strong communication skills to clearly and succinctly communicate model findings and limitations
Equivalent-circuit modeling fundamentals: parameter identification from pulse and drive-cycle data, and the physical basis (and limits) of R0/R1/C1 lumped elements.
CFD literacy sufficient to set up and diagnose a conjugate-heat-transfer problem: mesh independence, boundary conditions, convergence, residuals.
Fluent in Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib) for parameter extraction, correlation, and figure generation.
Willingness to complete GMPPU HV and cell-lab safety training on-site; prior HV lab exposure is a plus but not required.
Ability to work on-site in Concord, NC for the duration of the internship.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior Star-CCM+ experience (any module; Battery or conjugate heat-transfer preferred).
FSAE / Formula Student EV team involvement, especially battery pack or HV work.
MATLAB / Simulink literacy for cross-tool sanity checks.
Working knowledge of Li-ion cell electrochemistry fundamentals (OCV, polarization, thermal generation) sufficient to interpret ECM parameters physically.
Exposure to ISO 6469 or IEC 62660 test methodologies.
Coursework or research in electrochemistry, energy storage, or high-power-density thermal management.

Physical Requirements

Ability to stand, walk, and move in diverse operational environments, including race shops, arenas, and commercial facilities.
Comfortable working in variable environmental conditions, including loud, high-traffic, or high-pressure environments.

Why Join Us: You’ll help support a team developing a next-generation Formula 1 power unit, working alongside professionals who value precision, creativity, and a constant drive to improve. Interns will have the unique opportunity to work on a team poised to showcase American engineering excellence on the global Formula 1 stage.

High School diploma, GED, or equivalent education plus five years’ experience; OR Associate’s degree plus three years’ experience; OR Bachelor’s degree plus two years’ experience; OR Master’s degree in a related field plus one year’s experience, working in a human service setting; (E) and/or a mental health setting or with emotionally disturbed individuals. Work collaboratively with individuals identified as those with serious mental illness who meet the following criteria: histories of hospitalization, institutionalization, including with the criminal justice system, substance abuse, low engagement in medication treatment, and difficulty in participating in structured activities and living independently; (E)

title: SOCIAL SERVICE WORKER
description:
Home: Forest Heights, Long-term care
Position: Social Service Worker (SSW)
Salary Range: $29.00 per hour and $32.00 per hour
Status: Part-time (3 days/week), Vacancy
Southbridge Care Homes provides exceptional acquisition, management, and redevelopment services for long-term care homes and retirement communities across Ontario. Our mission is to maintain a best-in-class portfolio that consistently delivers excellence in care and services while ensuring economic sustainability.
Job Purpose: The Social Services Worker provides emotional, social, and practical support to residents and their families within the long-term care home. This role promotes resident well-being, dignity, and independence by addressing psychosocial needs, supporting transitions, and acting as a liaison between residents, families, staff, and community resources. The Social Worker ensures compliance with applicable legislation and professional standards while fostering a caring, resident-centred environment.
Reporting to: Executive Director
Key Responsibilities:

Coordinate, plan, and participate in annual and new admission interdisciplinary care conferences.
Develop and deliver social work services and programs to support the psychosocial needs of residents and their families/advocates.
Provide counseling, advocacy, and emotional support to residents and families as needed.
Provide palliative and end-of-life care support to residents and families.
Identify and respond to concerns of potential financial or emotional abuse, collaborating with the interdisciplinary team to address issues.
Lead the home’s ethics committee and provide consultation to staff on ethical dilemmas, working together to resolve concerns.
Participate in committees related to resident care and overall facility operations as required.
Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team to plan and coordinate resident-centered care.
Provide education and consultation on social work topics through staff orientation, ongoing training, and seminars for staff, residents, and families.
Maintain accurate and confidential documentation in compliance with the Long-Term Care Homes Act, professional standards, and organizational policies.
Connect residents and families with appropriate community services, government programs, and advocacy organizations.

Knowledge and Skills Required:

Bachelor/Masters of Social Work (BSW/MSW) or Social Service Worker (SSW)
Current registration and in good standing with the Ontario College of Social Workers or Social

Service Workers (or provincial equivalent).

Experience in long-term care, healthcare, or gerontology preferred.
Knowledge of the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, Residents’ Bill of Rights, and related regulations.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with a compassionate, resident-centered approach.
Ability to manage sensitive situations with empathy and professionalism.
Strong organizational and documentation skills.
Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team.
Knowledge of community resources, healthcare systems, and support services for seniors.

We would like to thank all applicants for your interest in working as part of our team! Only those applicants selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be contacted.
Southbridge welcomes those applicants with disability related needs and those whom a need for accommodation in the recruitment process. Please provide notice of your need for accommodation to the hiring manager upon scheduling of an interview.
At Southbridge, we care about your privacy and strive to protect Applicant Data throughout the recruitment process. To that end, information that we gather from applicants via job postings, is used solely for the purposes of recruiting and hiring.

Strong ability to support multiple projects simultaneously, with dependability and excellence. Understanding of The Austin Stone's ministry strategy and competency in application of strategies in equipping and mobilization. Able to manage a ministry budget.

title: Incentive Pay Analyst

The Finished Products Operator is responsible for safely forming a pulp sheet, cutting, preparing, packaging and loading the product on either railcars or trucks to ship the product to our customers. The Grande Prairie mill is an 1100+ tonne per day Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft pulp mill, employees approximately 400 mill employees in a 24-hour operation.

You are provided high quality, structured training and are highly compensated, including double time over time. Some OT is expected.
Profit sharing plan.
We are one of the safest mills in the world; we have a clean, warm work environment and have been in continuous production for 52 years.
We have opportunities for advancement in multiple disciplines and area’s.
We provide good health / dental benefits along with a pension plan.
Competitive vacation allotment and allow shift operations to bank Stat holidays to increase time off flexibility.
We have a highly engaged work force; you have the opportunity and will be expected to participate in improvement, as well as teams and committees. You have a say in how the work is done.
The shift schedule for this position is rotating 12-hour nights and days, with 14/28 days on shift. 7 days off straight each 28 days rotation.
